question: A financial services company is deploying a new application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application needs to read objects from an Amazon S3 bucket that contains sensitive customer data. The security team requires that no long-term credentials are stored on the instances and that access is limited to the minimum permissions required. What is the MOST secure way to grant the EC2 instances access to the S3 bucket?
options: A. Create an IAM user with an access key and secret key, store the keys in the application configuration file on each EC2 instance, and use those credentials in the AWS SDK.
B. Make the S3 bucket public and use unsigned requests from the application.
C. Create an IAM user, generate access keys, and store the keys in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as SecureString parameters. Retrieve the keys at application startup.
D. Create an IAM role with a policy that allows s3:GetObject on the specific bucket, attach the role to an instance profile, and associate the instance profile with the EC2 instances.

question: An organization is designing a multi-tier web application in a VPC. The application servers run in private subnets and need to download OS patches from the internet. The security team mandates that the servers must not have public IP addresses and that all outbound internet traffic must be controlled and logged. Which solution meets these requirements most securely?
options: A. Attach an internet gateway to the VPC and add a route to the internet gateway in the private subnet route tables.
B. Assign Elastic IP addresses to the application servers so they can reach the internet directly.
C. Deploy a NAT Gateway in a public subnet, update the private subnet route tables to point 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT Gateway, and enable VPC Flow Logs.
D. Create a VPC endpoint for every AWS service the servers might need and disable all internet access.

question: A healthcare company must ensure that all objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket are encrypted at rest using keys that the company fully controls and can rotate on demand. The company also wants the ability to disable a key immediately if compromise is suspected. Which solution should a Solutions Architect recommend?
options: A. Enable default encryption on the bucket using SSE-KMS with a customer managed key (CMK) in AWS KMS.
B. Require clients to encrypt objects client-side before uploading and store the keys in Amazon DynamoDB.
C. Use SSE-C and manage the encryption keys on the application servers.
D. Enable default encryption on the bucket using SSE-S3 (Amazon S3 managed keys).

question: An organization has multiple AWS accounts under AWS Organizations. The security team wants to prevent any account from creating Amazon S3 buckets that allow public access. They also want a centralized way to detect and remediate any existing public buckets. Which combination of services should be used?
options: A. Amazon GuardDuty and Amazon Macie only.
B. AWS CloudTrail and Amazon CloudWatch Alarms only.
C. IAM policies attached to every user denying public access actions.

D. Service Control Policies (SCPs) to deny s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock with public values, and AWS Config with the s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited and s3-bucket-public-write-prohibited managed rules plus automatic remediation.

question: An application running on Amazon ECS tasks needs to access a database password stored in AWS Secrets Manager. The tasks run in a private subnet with no internet access. How should the architecture be designed so that the tasks can retrieve the secret securely?
options: A. Use a NAT Gateway and allow the tasks to reach the public Secrets Manager endpoint.
B. Attach an internet gateway to the VPC so the tasks can reach the public Secrets Manager endpoint.
C. Store the password in an environment variable in the task definition.

D. Create an interface VPC endpoint for Secrets Manager in the VPC and attach a security group that allows HTTPS from the ECS tasks. Grant the task execution role permission to call secretsmanager:GetSecretValue.

question: A company is launching a public-facing web application behind an Application Load Balancer. The security team requires that only traffic from the corporate IP ranges can reach the administrative interface, while the main application remains publicly accessible. The administrative interface is hosted on the same ALB using a different path. What is the MOST efficient way to meet this requirement?
options: A. Place the administrative interface on a separate EC2 instance in a private subnet and use a bastion host.
B. Use AWS WAF on the ALB with an IP set match rule that allows the corporate CIDR ranges only for the administrative path, and allow all other traffic for the main application paths.
C. Create two separate Application Load Balancers — one public and one internal.
D. Modify the security group of the ALB to allow traffic only from the corporate IP ranges.

question: A Solutions Architect is designing authentication for a new SaaS application that will be used by employees of many different customer organizations. Each customer organization already has its own identity provider (IdP) that supports SAML 2.0. The application must allow users to sign in with their existing corporate credentials without creating separate IAM users. Which AWS service should be used?
options: A. AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO) with only the default identity source.
B. Amazon Cognito user pools with SAML identity provider federation.
C. IAM users and groups for every external employee.
D. Amazon Cognito identity pools without user pools.

question: A company stores sensitive documents in Amazon S3. They want to ensure that even the root user of the AWS account cannot permanently delete objects during a defined retention period. Which feature should be enabled?
options: A. S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode with a retention period.
B. S3 Lifecycle rules that transition objects to Glacier.
C. S3 Versioning only.
D. MFA Delete on the bucket.

question: A web application uses an Application Load Balancer and Amazon EC2 instances. The security team has detected that attackers are attempting SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks. Which AWS service should be deployed to protect the application with minimal changes to the existing architecture?
options: A. AWS WAF associated with the Application Load Balancer, using AWS Managed Rules for common threats.
B. AWS Shield Advanced only.
C. Network ACLs with deny rules for all suspicious IP addresses.
D. Amazon Inspector on the EC2 instances.

question: An organization runs workloads in multiple AWS accounts. Developers in a development account need temporary access to read objects in a production S3 bucket. The access must be time-limited and auditable. What is the MOST secure approach?
options: A. Make the production S3 bucket public with a bucket policy that allows the development account.

B. Create an IAM role in the production account that trusts the development account, attach a least-privilege policy for S3 read access, and allow developers to assume the role using STS. Enable CloudTrail logging.
C. Create a long-lived IAM user in the production account and share the access keys with the developers.
D. Copy the required objects to the development account every night.

question: An application running on Amazon EC2 needs to call Amazon DynamoDB. The security team requires that the traffic never leaves the Amazon network and that no public endpoints are used. How should this be configured?
options: A. Use the public DynamoDB endpoint and rely on HTTPS.
B. Deploy a NAT Gateway and force all traffic through it.
C. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB and update the route table of the subnet where the EC2 instances reside so that DynamoDB traffic is routed through the endpoint.
D. Use an interface VPC endpoint for DynamoDB and place it in a public subnet.

question: A company wants to enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for any IAM user that attempts to stop or terminate Amazon EC2 instances. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: A. Use Amazon Cognito for all EC2 management.
B. Attach an IAM policy to all users that includes a condition key aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent set to true for the ec2:StopInstances and ec2:TerminateInstances actions.
C. Configure MFA at the VPC level using network ACLs.
D. Enable MFA only on the root user.

question: A cloud architect must design a solution that logs all API activity across every AWS account in an organization and retains the logs for 7 years for compliance. The solution must also protect the logs from tampering. Which architecture should be recommended?
options: A. Create an organization trail in the management account that delivers logs to a central S3 bucket in a dedicated log archive account. Enable log file integrity validation and apply an S3 bucket policy that denies delete and overwrite actions to all principals except a designated audit role.
B. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs only and set retention to 7 years.
C. Enable VPC Flow Logs in every VPC and store them in CloudWatch Logs.
D. Enable AWS CloudTrail in each account separately and store logs in the same account.

question: A company is migrating an application that currently uses a shared database username and password embedded in configuration files. They want to eliminate hard-coded credentials and automatically rotate the password every 30 days. Which AWS service combination is the MOST appropriate?
options: A. Store the password in Amazon S3 and retrieve it at runtime.

B. Use AWS Secrets Manager to store the database credentials, enable automatic rotation with a Lambda rotation function, and update the application to retrieve the secret at runtime using the AWS SDK.
C. Store the password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as a standard parameter and rotate it manually.
D. Create an IAM database user and use IAM authentication only.

question: A public website is hosted on Amazon S3 and fronted by Amazon CloudFront. The company wants to ensure that users can access the content only through CloudFront and never by using the S3 website endpoint or the S3 REST endpoint directly. How should this be enforced?
options: A. Make the S3 bucket public and rely on CloudFront cache behaviors.
B. Enable S3 Block Public Access and remove the bucket policy entirely.
C. Use a security group on the S3 bucket.

D. Create an Origin Access Control (OAC) or Origin Access Identity (OAI) for CloudFront, update the S3 bucket policy to allow access only from the CloudFront service principal / OAI, and deny all other principals.

question: An organization needs to allow developers to launch Amazon EC2 instances, but they must only be allowed to launch instances that use encrypted EBS volumes. Which combination of controls should be implemented?
options: A. A network ACL that blocks unencrypted volumes.
B. An S3 bucket policy.
C. An IAM policy that denies ec2:RunInstances when the ebs:Encrypted condition is false, and optionally an AWS Config rule to detect non-compliant instances.
D. A security group rule that requires encryption.

question: An application uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The database contains personal data that must be encrypted at rest. The company also wants to use a customer managed key so they can control key rotation and access. What should the Solutions Architect do?
options: A. Create a new encrypted RDS instance using a customer managed KMS key (CMK), migrate the data, and update the application connection string.
B. Use client-side encryption only and leave the RDS instance unencrypted.
C. Enable encryption with the default AWS managed key and never use a CMK.
D. Enable encryption on an existing unencrypted RDS instance using the modify command.

question: An organization has a requirement that all traffic between its Application Load Balancer and the backend EC2 instances must be encrypted in transit. The ALB currently terminates SSL and forwards HTTP to the targets. What change is required?
options: A. Use a Network Load Balancer instead of an Application Load Balancer.

B. Configure the target group to use the HTTPS protocol, install certificates on the EC2 instances (or use ACM certificates where supported), and update the security groups to allow traffic on the HTTPS port.
C. Leave the configuration as-is; SSL termination at the ALB is sufficient.
D. Enable sticky sessions only.

question: A Solutions Architect is reviewing the security of an existing VPC. The VPC has both public and private subnets. The private subnets currently route all outbound traffic (0.0.0.0/0) through a NAT Gateway. The security team wants to ensure that the private instances can reach Amazon S3 without going through the NAT Gateway, to reduce cost and attack surface. What is the BEST solution?
options: A. Add an internet gateway route to the private subnets.
B. Move the instances to public subnets and assign public IP addresses.
C. Create an interface VPC endpoint for S3.
D. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for S3 and add a route in the private subnet route tables that directs S3 traffic to the endpoint.

question: A company wants to detect unusual API activity, such as an IAM user creating multiple access keys or disabling CloudTrail, across all accounts in its AWS Organization. Which service is designed for this continuous threat detection use case?
options: A. AWS Config
B. Amazon GuardDuty with a delegated administrator in the organization
C. Amazon Inspector
D. AWS Trusted Advisor

question: An application needs temporary credentials to access AWS resources. The application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Which mechanism provides the MOST secure short-lived credentials?
options: A. Hard-coded root account credentials.
B. Long-lived access keys rotated every 90 days and stored in environment variables.
C. IAM user access keys stored in the instance metadata or configuration files.
D. An IAM role attached to the instance via an instance profile; the application retrieves temporary credentials from the instance metadata service (IMDSv2 recommended).

question: A company is implementing a zero-trust network model for its VPC. They want to control traffic between application tiers (web, application, database) using identity-aware policies rather than only IP-based rules. Which AWS service can help implement this?
options: A. AWS Verified Access or Amazon VPC Lattice with authentication policies, combined with security groups.
B. Only network ACLs with deny rules.
C. AWS WAF on every instance.
D. Security groups and network ACLs only.

question: A Solutions Architect must ensure that Amazon CloudWatch Logs data is encrypted at rest using a customer managed key. How can this be achieved?
options: A. Store the logs only in Amazon S3 and never use CloudWatch Logs.
B. Associate a customer managed KMS key with the CloudWatch Logs log group when it is created or by updating the log group.
C. Encrypt the logs client-side before sending them to CloudWatch.
D. CloudWatch Logs is always encrypted with an AWS owned key and cannot use a CMK.

question: An organization has an Amazon RDS MySQL database that must be accessible only from application servers running in a specific private subnet. Database administrators also need occasional access from a bastion host. How should network access be controlled?
options: A. Place the RDS instance in a private subnet, create a security group for RDS that allows inbound MySQL traffic only from the security groups of the application servers and the bastion host.
B. Allow inbound traffic from the entire VPC CIDR on the RDS security group.
C. Use network ACLs only and leave the security group open.
D. Place the RDS instance in a public subnet and use a security group that allows 0.0.0.0/0 on port 3306.

question: A company wants to share an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) with another AWS account while ensuring that the AMI cannot be further shared or made public by the receiving account. What is the correct approach?
options: A. Export the AMI to S3 and share the S3 bucket publicly.
B. Share the AMI with the specific AWS account ID and, if needed, use AWS Organizations or License Manager controls; for encrypted AMIs also share the KMS key.
C. Make the AMI public.
D. Copy the AMI to the other account using the AWS Management Console without any restrictions.

question: An organization is subject to strict compliance requirements that mandate encryption of all data in transit and at rest, plus detailed logging of access to sensitive data. They are storing the data in Amazon S3. Which combination of features should be enabled?
options: A. SSE-S3 only and CloudTrail data events for S3.
B. Versioning and MFA Delete only.

C. Default encryption with a customer managed KMS key (SSE-KMS), S3 server access logging or CloudTrail data events, and a bucket policy that denies unencrypted uploads (s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption condition).
D. Client-side encryption only with no server-side encryption.

question: An organization runs a three-tier application. The database tier is Amazon RDS. The security team requires that the database credentials used by the application tier are never stored in plain text in the application configuration or environment variables. What is the recommended solution?
options: A. Retrieve the credentials at runtime from AWS Secrets Manager (or SSM Parameter Store SecureString) using an IAM role attached to the application instances, and enable automatic rotation if possible.
B. Store the credentials in a plain-text file on the EBS volume of the application servers.
C. Pass the credentials as command-line arguments when launching the application.
D. Hard-code the credentials in the application source code and re-deploy when they change.

question: A Solutions Architect needs to design a solution that prevents any IAM user or role in a member account from disabling AWS CloudTrail or deleting CloudTrail logs. The accounts are part of an AWS Organization. What is the MOST effective control?
options: A. A CloudWatch Alarm that notifies when CloudTrail is disabled.
B. An IAM policy in each account that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging and s3:DeleteObject on the log bucket.
C. Amazon GuardDuty findings only.

D. A Service Control Policy (SCP) attached to the organization or organizational units that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, and s3:DeleteObject / s3:PutBucketPolicy on the central log bucket, combined with a central organization trail.

question: An application hosted on Amazon EC2 needs to access objects in an S3 bucket. The company wants to ensure that the traffic between the EC2 instances and S3 does not traverse the public internet and does not require a NAT Gateway. The instances are in a private subnet. Which solution should be implemented?
options: A. Create an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 and place it in a public subnet.
B. Use AWS PrivateLink with a Network Load Balancer in front of S3.
C. Assign public IP addresses to the EC2 instances.
D. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 and add the appropriate route to the private subnet route table.

question: A company is building a multi-account environment using AWS Control Tower. They want to ensure that every new account has a baseline set of security controls, including mandatory CloudTrail logging, Config rules, and restricted root user usage. Which feature of Control Tower helps enforce this?
options: A. Amazon Macie automatically enabled in every account.
B. Account Factory and Guardrails (both preventive and detective).
C. Only the AWS Organizations management account console.
D. Manual IAM policies applied after account creation.

options: A. Copy the AMI to the other account using the AWS Management Console without any restrictions.
B. Make the AMI public.
C. Share the AMI with the specific AWS account ID and, if needed, use AWS Organizations or License Manager controls; for encrypted AMIs also share the KMS key.
D. Export the AMI to S3 and share the S3 bucket publicly.

question: An organization is subject to strict compliance requirements that mandate encryption of all data in transit and at rest, plus detailed logging of access to sensitive data. They are storing the data in Amazon S3. Which combination of features should be enabled?
options: A. SSE-S3 only and CloudTrail data events for S3.
B. Client-side encryption only with no server-side encryption.

C. Default encryption with a customer managed KMS key (SSE-KMS), S3 server access logging or CloudTrail data events, and a bucket policy that denies unencrypted uploads (s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption condition).
D. Versioning and MFA Delete only.

question: A company runs a three-tier application. The database tier is Amazon RDS. The security team requires that the database credentials used by the application tier are never stored in plain text in the application configuration or environment variables. What is the recommended solution?
options: A. Store the credentials in a plain-text file on the EBS volume of the application servers.
B. Pass the credentials as command-line arguments when launching the application.

C. Retrieve the credentials at runtime from AWS Secrets Manager (or SSM Parameter Store SecureString) using an IAM role attached to the application instances, and enable automatic rotation if possible.
D. Hard-code the credentials in the application source code and re-deploy when they change.

question: A Solutions Architect needs to design a solution that prevents any IAM user or role in a member account from disabling AWS CloudTrail or deleting CloudTrail logs. The accounts are part of an AWS Organization. What is the MOST effective control?
options: A. An IAM policy in each account that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging and s3:DeleteObject on the log bucket.
B. A CloudWatch Alarm that notifies when CloudTrail is disabled.
C. Amazon GuardDuty findings only.

D. A Service Control Policy (SCP) attached to the organization or organizational units that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, and s3:DeleteObject / s3:PutBucketPolicy on the central log bucket, combined with a central organization trail.

question: An application hosted on Amazon EC2 needs to access objects in an S3 bucket. The company wants to ensure that the traffic between the EC2 instances and S3 does not traverse the public internet and does not require a NAT Gateway. The instances are in a private subnet. Which solution should be implemented?
options: A. Assign public IP addresses to the EC2 instances.
B. Use AWS PrivateLink with a Network Load Balancer in front of S3.
C. Create an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 and place it in a public subnet.
D. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 and add the appropriate route to the private subnet route table.

question: An organization is building a multi-account environment using AWS Control Tower. They want to ensure that every new account has a baseline set of security controls, including mandatory CloudTrail logging, Config rules, and restricted root user usage. Which feature of Control Tower helps enforce this?
options: A. Only the AWS Organizations management account console.
B. Account Factory and Guardrails (both preventive and detective).
C. Manual IAM policies applied after account creation.
D. Amazon Macie automatically enabled in every account.

question: A financial services company is deploying a new application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application needs to read objects from an Amazon S3 bucket that contains sensitive customer data. The security team requires that no long-term credentials are stored on the instances and that access is limited to the minimum permissions required. What is the most secure way to grant the EC2 instances access to the S3 bucket?
options: A. Create an IAM user with an access key and secret key, store the keys in the application configuration file on each EC2 instance, and use those credentials in the AWS SDK.
B. Create an IAM role with a policy that allows s3:GetObject on the specific bucket, attach the role to an instance profile, and associate the instance profile with the EC2 instances.
C. Create an IAM user, generate access keys, and store the keys in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as SecureString parameters. Retrieve the keys at application startup.
D. Make the S3 bucket public and use unsigned requests from the application.

question: A company is designing a multi-tier web application in a VPC. The application servers run in private subnets and need to download OS patches from the internet. The security team mandates that the servers must not have public IP addresses and that all outbound internet traffic must be controlled and logged. Which solution meets these requirements MOST securely?
options: A. Create a VPC endpoint for every AWS service the servers might need and disable all internet access.
B. Attach an internet gateway to the VPC and add a route to the internet gateway in the private subnet route tables.
C. Deploy a NAT Gateway in a public subnet, update the private subnet route tables to point 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT Gateway, and enable VPC Flow Logs.
D. Assign Elastic IP addresses to the application servers so they can reach the internet directly.

question: A healthcare company must ensure that all objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket are encrypted at rest using keys that the company fully controls and can rotate on demand. The company also wants the ability to disable a key immediately if compromise is suspected. Which solution should a Solutions Architect recommend?
options: A. Use SSE-C and manage the encryption keys on the application servers.
B. Enable default encryption on the bucket using SSE-KMS with a customer managed key (CMK) in AWS KMS.
C. Require clients to encrypt objects client-side before uploading and store the keys in Amazon DynamoDB.
D. Enable default encryption on the bucket using SSE-S3 (Amazon S3 managed keys).

question: A company has multiple AWS accounts under AWS Organizations. The security team wants to prevent any account from creating Amazon S3 buckets that allow public access. They also want a centralized way to detect and remediate any existing public buckets. Which combination of services should be used?
options: A. IAM policies attached to every user denying public access actions.

B. Service Control Policies (SCPs) to deny s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock with public values, and AWS Config with the s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited and s3-bucket-public-write-prohibited managed rules plus automatic remediation.
C. AWS CloudTrail and Amazon CloudWatch Alarms only.
D. Amazon GuardDuty and Amazon Macie only.

question: An application running on Amazon ECS tasks needs to access a database password stored in AWS Secrets Manager. The tasks run in a private subnet with no internet access. How should the architecture be designed so that the tasks can retrieve the secret securely?
options: A. Create an interface VPC endpoint for Secrets Manager in the VPC and attach a security group that allows HTTPS from the ECS tasks. Grant the task execution role permission to call secretsmanager:GetSecretValue.
B. Store the password in an environment variable in the task definition.
C. Attach an internet gateway to the VPC so the tasks can reach the public Secrets Manager endpoint.
D. Use a NAT Gateway and allow the tasks to reach the public Secrets Manager endpoint.

question: A company is launching a public-facing web application behind an Application Load Balancer. The security team requires that only traffic from the corporate IP ranges can reach the administrative interface, while the main application remains publicly accessible. The administrative interface is hosted on the same ALB using a different path. What is the MOST efficient way to meet this requirement?
options: A. Place the administrative interface on a separate EC2 instance in a private subnet and use a bastion host.
B. Modify the security group of the ALB to allow traffic only from the corporate IP ranges.
C. Use AWS WAF on the ALB with an IP set match rule that allows the corporate CIDR ranges only for the administrative path, and allow all other traffic for the main application paths.
D. Create two separate Application Load Balancers — one public and one internal.

question: A Solutions Architect is designing authentication for a new SaaS application that will be used by employees of many different customer organizations. Each customer organization already has its own identity provider (IdP) that supports SAML 2.0. The application must allow users to sign in with their existing corporate credentials without creating separate IAM users. Which AWS service should be used?
options: A. IAM users and groups for every external employee.
B. Amazon Cognito user pools with SAML identity provider federation.
C. Amazon Cognito identity pools without user pools.
D. AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO) with only the default identity source.

question: A company stores sensitive documents in Amazon S3. They want to ensure that even the root user of the AWS account cannot permanently delete objects during a defined retention period. Which feature should be enabled?
options: A. MFA Delete on the bucket.
B. S3 Lifecycle rules that transition objects to Glacier.
C. S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode with a retention period.
D. S3 Versioning only.

question: A web application uses an Application Load Balancer and Amazon EC2 instances. The security team has detected that attackers are attempting SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks. Which AWS service should be deployed to protect the application with minimal changes to the existing architecture?
options: A. AWS Shield Advanced only.
B. AWS WAF associated with the Application Load Balancer, using AWS Managed Rules for common threats.
C. Network ACLs with deny rules for all suspicious IP addresses.
D. Amazon Inspector on the EC2 instances.

question: An organization runs workloads in multiple AWS accounts. Developers in a development account need temporary access to read objects in a production S3 bucket. The access must be time-limited and auditable. What is the most secure approach?
options: A. Make the production S3 bucket public with a bucket policy that allows the development account.
B. Copy the required objects to the development account every night.

C. Create an IAM role in the production account that trusts the development account, attach a least-privilege policy for S3 read access, and allow developers to assume the role using STS. Enable CloudTrail logging.
D. Create a long-lived IAM user in the production account and share the access keys with the developers.

question: An application running on Amazon EC2 needs to call Amazon DynamoDB. The security team requires that the traffic never leaves the Amazon network and that no public endpoints are used. How should this be configured?
options: A. Use the public DynamoDB endpoint and rely on HTTPS.
B. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB and update the route table of the subnet where the EC2 instances reside so that DynamoDB traffic is routed through the endpoint.
C. Use an interface VPC endpoint for DynamoDB and place it in a public subnet.
D. Deploy a NAT Gateway and force all traffic through it.

question: A company wants to enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for any IAM user that attempts to stop or terminate Amazon EC2 instances. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: A. Use Amazon Cognito for all EC2 management.
B. Attach an IAM policy to all users that includes a condition key aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent set to true for the ec2:StopInstances and ec2:TerminateInstances actions.
C. Enable MFA only on the root user.
D. Configure MFA at the VPC level using network ACLs.

question: A cloud architect must design a solution that logs all API activity across every AWS account in an organization and retains the logs for 7 years for compliance. The solution must also protect the logs from tampering. Which architecture should be recommended?

B. Enable VPC Flow Logs in every VPC and store them in CloudWatch Logs.

question: A company is migrating an application that currently uses a shared database username and password embedded in configuration files. They want to eliminate hard-coded credentials and automatically rotate the password every 30 days. Which AWS service combination is the MOST appropriate?
options: A. Store the password in Amazon S3 and retrieve it at runtime.
B. Store the password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as a standard parameter and rotate it manually.
C. Create an IAM database user and use IAM authentication only.

D. Use AWS Secrets Manager to store the database credentials, enable automatic rotation with a Lambda rotation function, and update the application to retrieve the secret at runtime using the AWS SDK.

question: A public website is hosted on Amazon S3 and fronted by Amazon CloudFront. The company wants to ensure that users can access the content only through CloudFront and never by using the S3 website endpoint or the S3 REST endpoint directly. How should this be enforced?

C. Enable S3 Block Public Access and remove the bucket policy entirely.
D. Use a security group on the S3 bucket.

question: A company needs to allow developers to launch Amazon EC2 instances, but they must only be allowed to launch instances that use encrypted EBS volumes. Which combination of controls should be implemented?

C. A network ACL that blocks unencrypted volumes.
D. A security group rule that requires encryption.

question: An application uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The database contains personal data that must be encrypted at rest. The company also wants to use a customer managed key so they can control key rotation and access. What should the Solutions Architect do?

question: An organization has a requirement that all traffic between its Application Load Balancer and the backend EC2 instances must be encrypted in transit. The ALB currently terminates SSL and forwards HTTP to the targets. What change is required?

B. Enable sticky sessions only.
C. Use a Network Load Balancer instead of an Application Load Balancer.

D. Configure the target group to use the HTTPS protocol, install certificates on the EC2 instances (or use ACM certificates where supported), and update the security groups to allow traffic on the HTTPS port.

question: A Solutions Architect is reviewing the security of an existing VPC. The VPC has both public and private subnets. The private subnets currently route all outbound traffic (0.0.0.0/0) through a NAT Gateway. options: A. Move the instances to public subnets and assign public IP addresses.
B. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for S3 and add a route in the private subnet route tables that directs S3 traffic to the endpoint.
C. Create an interface VPC endpoint for S3.
D. Add an internet gateway route to the private subnets.

question: An organization wants to detect unusual API activity, such as an IAM user creating multiple access keys or disabling CloudTrail, across all accounts in its AWS Organization. Which service is designed for this continuous threat detection use case?
options: A. Amazon Inspector
B. AWS Config
C. Amazon GuardDuty with a delegated administrator in the organization

B. AWS WAF on every instance.

question: A Solutions Architect must ensure that Amazon CloudWatch Logs data is encrypted at rest using a customer managed key. How can this be achieved?
options: A. CloudWatch Logs is always encrypted with an AWS owned key and cannot use a CMK.

question: A company has an Amazon RDS MySQL database that must be accessible only from application servers running in a specific private subnet. Database administrators also need occasional access from a bastion host. How should network access be controlled?

options: A. Leave the configuration as-is; SSL termination at the ALB is sufficient.
B. Enable sticky sessions only.
C. Use a Network Load Balancer instead of an Application Load Balancer.

D. Configure the target group to use the HTTPS protocol, install certificates on the EC2 instances (or use ACM certificates where supported), and update the security groups to allow traffic on the HTTPS port.

question: A Solutions Architect is reviewing the security of an existing VPC. The VPC has both public and private subnets. The private subnets currently route all outbound traffic (0.0.0.0/0) through a NAT Gateway. The security team wants to ensure that the private instances can reach Amazon S3 without going through the NAT Gateway, to reduce cost and attack surface. What is the BEST solution?
options: A. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for S3 and add a route in the private subnet route tables that directs S3 traffic to the endpoint.
B. Add an internet gateway route to the private subnets.
C. Create an interface VPC endpoint for S3.
D. Move the instances to public subnets and assign public IP addresses.

question: An organization wants to detect unusual API activity, such as an IAM user creating multiple access keys or disabling CloudTrail, across all accounts in its AWS Organization. Which service is designed for this continuous threat detection use case?
options: A. AWS Config
B. AWS Trusted Advisor
C. Amazon GuardDuty with a delegated administrator in the organization
D. Amazon Inspector

question: An application needs temporary credentials to access AWS resources. The application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Which mechanism provides the MOST secure short-lived credentials?
options: A. Long-lived access keys rotated every 90 days and stored in environment variables.
B. Hard-coded root account credentials.
C. An IAM role attached to the instance via an instance profile; the application retrieves temporary credentials from the instance metadata service (IMDSv2 recommended).
D. IAM user access keys stored in the instance metadata or configuration files.

question: A company is implementing a zero-trust network model for its VPC. They want to control traffic between application tiers (web, application, database) using identity-aware policies rather than only IP-based rules. Which AWS service can help implement this?
options: A. Security groups and network ACLs only.
B. Only network ACLs with deny rules.
C. AWS Verified Access or Amazon VPC Lattice with authentication policies, combined with security groups.
D. AWS WAF on every instance.

question: A Solutions Architect must ensure that Amazon CloudWatch Logs data is encrypted at rest using a customer managed key. How can this be achieved?
options: A. CloudWatch Logs is always encrypted with an AWS owned key and cannot use a CMK.
B. Store the logs only in Amazon S3 and never use CloudWatch Logs.
C. Encrypt the logs client-side before sending them to CloudWatch.
D. Associate a customer managed KMS key with the CloudWatch Logs log group when it is created or by updating the log group.

question: A company has an Amazon RDS MySQL database that must be accessible only from application servers running in a specific private subnet. Database administrators also need occasional access from a bastion host. How should network access be controlled?
options: A. Place the RDS instance in a public subnet and use a security group that allows 0.0.0.0/0 on port 3306.
B. Place the RDS instance in a private subnet, create a security group for RDS that allows inbound MySQL traffic only from the security groups of the application servers and the bastion host.
C. Allow inbound traffic from the entire VPC CIDR on the RDS security group.
D. Use network ACLs only and leave the security group open.

question: A company wants to share an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) with another AWS account while ensuring that the AMI cannot be further shared or made public by the receiving account. What is the correct approach?
options: A. Export the AMI to S3 and share the S3 bucket publicly.
B. Copy the AMI to the other account using the AWS Management Console without any restrictions.
C. Share the AMI with the specific AWS account ID and, if needed, use AWS Organizations or License Manager controls; for encrypted AMIs also share the KMS key.
D. Make the AMI public.

question: An organization is subject to strict compliance requirements that mandate encryption of all data in transit and at rest, plus detailed logging of access to sensitive data. They are storing the data in Amazon S3. Which combination of features should be enabled?
options: A. Default encryption with a customer managed KMS key (SSE-KMS), S3 server access logging or CloudTrail data events, and a bucket policy that denies unencrypted uploads (s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption condition).
B. SSE-S3 only and CloudTrail data events for S3.
C. Versioning and MFA Delete only.
D. Client-side encryption only with no server-side encryption.

question: A company runs a three-tier application. The database tier is Amazon RDS. The security team requires that the database credentials used by the application tier are never stored in plain text in the application configuration or environment variables. What is the recommended solution?
options: A. Hard-code the credentials in the application source code and re-deploy when they change.

B. Retrieve the credentials at runtime from AWS Secrets Manager (or SSM Parameter Store SecureString) using an IAM role attached to the application instances, and enable automatic rotation if possible.
C. Store the credentials in a plain-text file on the EBS volume of the application servers.
D. Pass the credentials as command-line arguments when launching the application.

question: A Solutions Architect needs to design a solution that prevents any IAM user or role in a member account from disabling AWS CloudTrail or deleting CloudTrail logs. The accounts are part of an AWS Organization. What is the MOST effective control?
options: A. A Service Control Policy (SCP) attached to the organization or organizational units that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, and s3:DeleteObject / s3:PutBucketPolicy on the central log bucket, combined with a central organization trail.
B. A CloudWatch Alarm that notifies when CloudTrail is disabled.
C. Amazon GuardDuty findings only.
D. An IAM policy in each account that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging and s3:DeleteObject on the log bucket.

question: An application hosted on Amazon EC2 needs to access objects in an S3 bucket. The company wants to ensure that the traffic between the EC2 instances and S3 does not traverse the public internet and does not require a NAT Gateway. The instances are in a private subnet. Which solution should be implemented?
options: A. Assign public IP addresses to the EC2 instances.
B. Use AWS PrivateLink with a Network Load Balancer in front of S3.
C. Create an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 and place it in a public subnet.
D. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 and add the appropriate route to the private subnet route table.

question: A company is building a multi-account environment using AWS Control Tower. They want to ensure that every new account has a baseline set of security controls, including mandatory CloudTrail logging, Config rules, and restricted root user usage. Which feature of Control Tower helps enforce this?
options: A. Account Factory and Guardrails (both preventive and detective).
B. Manual IAM policies applied after account creation.
C. Amazon Macie automatically enabled in every account.
D. Only the AWS Organizations management account console.

question: A financial services company is deploying a new application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application needs to read objects from an Amazon S3 bucket that contains sensitive customer data. The security team requires that no long-term credentials are stored on the instances and that access is limited to the minimum permissions required. What is the MOST secure way to grant the EC2 instances access to the S3 bucket?
options: A. Create an IAM user with an access key and secret key, store the keys in the application configuration file on each EC2 instance, and use those credentials in the AWS SDK.
B. Make the S3 bucket public and use unsigned requests from the application.
C. Create an IAM role with a policy that allows s3:GetObject on the specific bucket, attach the role to an instance profile, and associate the instance profile with the EC2 instances.
D. Create an IAM user, generate access keys, and store the keys in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as SecureString parameters. Retrieve the keys at application startup.

question: A company is designing a multi-tier web application in a VPC. The application servers run in private subnets and need to download OS patches from the internet. The security team mandates that the servers must not have public IP addresses and that all outbound internet traffic must be controlled and logged. Which solution meets these requirements MOST securely?
options: A. Assign Elastic IP addresses to the application servers so they can reach the internet directly.
B. Deploy a NAT Gateway in a public subnet, update the private subnet route tables to point 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT Gateway, and enable VPC Flow Logs.
C. Attach an internet gateway to the VPC and add a route to the internet gateway in the private subnet route tables.
D. Create a VPC endpoint for every AWS service the servers might need and disable all internet access.

question: A healthcare company must ensure that all objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket are encrypted at rest using keys that the company fully controls and can rotate on demand. The company also wants the ability to disable a key immediately if compromise is suspected. Which solution should a Solutions Architect recommend?
options: A. Enable default encryption on the bucket using SSE-KMS with a customer managed key (CMK) in AWS KMS.
B. Require clients to encrypt objects client-side before uploading and store the keys in Amazon DynamoDB.
C. Use SSE-C and manage the encryption keys on the application servers.
D. Enable default encryption on the bucket using SSE-S3 (Amazon S3 managed keys).

question: A company has multiple AWS accounts under AWS Organizations. The security team wants to prevent any account from creating Amazon S3 buckets that allow public access. They also want a centralized way to detect and remediate any existing public buckets. Which combination of services should be used?
options: A. AWS CloudTrail and Amazon CloudWatch Alarms only.
B. Amazon GuardDuty and Amazon Macie only.
C. IAM policies attached to every user denying public access actions.

D. Service Control Policies (SCPs) to deny s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock with public values, and AWS Config with the s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited and s3-bucket-public-write-prohibited managed rules plus automatic remediation.

question: An application running on Amazon ECS tasks needs to access a database password stored in AWS Secrets Manager. The tasks run in a private subnet with no internet access. How should the architecture be designed so that the tasks can retrieve the secret securely?
options: A. Create an interface VPC endpoint for Secrets Manager in the VPC and attach a security group that allows HTTPS from the ECS tasks. Grant the task execution role permission to call secretsmanager:GetSecretValue.
B. Store the password in an environment variable in the task definition.
C. Use a NAT Gateway and allow the tasks to reach the public Secrets Manager endpoint.
D. Attach an internet gateway to the VPC so the tasks can reach the public Secrets Manager endpoint.

question: A company is launching a public-facing web application behind an Application Load Balancer. The security team requires that only traffic from the corporate IP ranges can reach the administrative interface, while the main application remains publicly accessible. The administrative interface is hosted on the same ALB using a different path. What is the MOST efficient way to meet this requirement?
options: A. Create two separate Application Load Balancers — one public and one internal.
B. Place the administrative interface on a separate EC2 instance in a private subnet and use a bastion host.
C. Use AWS WAF on the ALB with an IP set match rule that allows the corporate CIDR ranges only for the administrative path, and allow all other traffic for the main application paths.
D. Modify the security group of the ALB to allow traffic only from the corporate IP ranges.

question: A Solutions Architect is designing authentication for a new SaaS application that will be used by employees of many different customer organizations. Each customer organization already has its own identity provider (IdP) that supports SAML 2.0. The application must allow users to sign in with their existing corporate credentials without creating separate IAM users. Which AWS service should be used?
options: A. AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO) with only the default identity source.
B. Amazon Cognito identity pools without user pools.
C. IAM users and groups for every external employee.
D. Amazon Cognito user pools with SAML identity provider federation.

question: A company stores sensitive documents in Amazon S3. They want to ensure that even the root user of the AWS account cannot permanently delete objects during a defined retention period. Which feature should be enabled?
options: A. S3 Versioning only.
B. S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode with a retention period.
C. MFA Delete on the bucket.
D. S3 Lifecycle rules that transition objects to Glacier.

question: A web application uses an Application Load Balancer and Amazon EC2 instances. The security team has detected that attackers are attempting SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks. Which AWS service should be deployed to protect the application with minimal changes to the existing architecture?
options: A. AWS Shield Advanced only.
B. Amazon Inspector on the EC2 instances.
C. Network ACLs with deny rules for all suspicious IP addresses.
D. AWS WAF associated with the Application Load Balancer, using AWS Managed Rules for common threats.

question: A company runs workloads in multiple AWS accounts. Developers in a development account need temporary access to read objects in a production S3 bucket. The access must be time-limited and auditable. What is the MOST secure approach?
options: A. Copy the required objects to the development account every night.
B. Make the production S3 bucket public with a bucket policy that allows the development account.

C. Create an IAM role in the production account that trusts the development account, attach a least-privilege policy for S3 read access, and allow developers to assume the role using STS. Enable CloudTrail logging.
D. Create a long-lived IAM user in the production account and share the access keys with the developers.

question: An application running on Amazon EC2 needs to call Amazon DynamoDB. The security team requires that the traffic never leaves the Amazon network and that no public endpoints are used. How should this be configured?
options: A. Use an interface VPC endpoint for DynamoDB and place it in a public subnet.
B. Use the public DynamoDB endpoint and rely on HTTPS.
C. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB and update the route table of the subnet where the EC2 instances reside so that DynamoDB traffic is routed through the endpoint.
D. Deploy a NAT Gateway and force all traffic through it.

question: A company wants to enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for any IAM user that attempts to stop or terminate Amazon EC2 instances. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: A. Attach an IAM policy to all users that includes a condition key aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent set to true for the ec2:StopInstances and ec2:TerminateInstances actions.
B. Use Amazon Cognito for all EC2 management.
C. Configure MFA at the VPC level using network ACLs.
D. Enable MFA only on the root user.

question: A Solutions Architect must design a solution that logs all API activity across every AWS account in an organization and retains the logs for 7 years for compliance. The solution must also protect the logs from tampering. Which architecture should be recommended?

B. Enable VPC Flow Logs in every VPC and store them in CloudWatch Logs.
C. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs only and set retention to 7 years.

D. Create an organization trail in the management account that delivers logs to a central S3 bucket in a dedicated log archive account. Enable log file integrity validation and apply an S3 bucket policy that denies delete and overwrite actions to all principals except a designated audit role.

question: A company is migrating an application that currently uses a shared database username and password embedded in configuration files. They want to eliminate hard-coded credentials and automatically rotate the password every 30 days. Which AWS service combination is the MOST appropriate?

D. Store the password in Amazon S3 and retrieve it at runtime.

question: A public website is hosted on Amazon S3 and fronted by Amazon CloudFront. The company wants to ensure that users can access the content only through CloudFront and never by using the S3 website endpoint or the S3 REST endpoint directly. How should this be enforced?

question: A company needs to allow developers to launch Amazon EC2 instances, but they must only be allowed to launch instances that use encrypted EBS volumes. Which combination of controls should be implemented?
options: A. An IAM policy that denies ec2:RunInstances when the ebs:Encrypted condition is false, and optionally an AWS Config rule to detect non-compliant instances.

C. A network ACL that blocks unencrypted volumes.
D. An S3 bucket policy.

question: An application uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The database contains personal data that must be encrypted at rest. The company also wants to use a customer managed key so they can control key rotation and access. What should the Solutions Architect do?
options: A. Enable encryption on an existing unencrypted RDS instance using the modify command.

question: A company wants to enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for any IAM user that attempts to stop or terminate Amazon EC2 instances. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: A. Use Amazon Cognito for all EC2 management.
B. Enable MFA only on the root user.
C. Configure MFA at the VPC level using network ACLs.
D. Attach an IAM policy to all users that includes a condition key aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent set to true for the ec2:StopInstances and ec2:TerminateInstances actions.

question: A Solutions Architect must design a solution that logs all API activity across every AWS account in an organization and retains the logs for 7 years for compliance. The solution must also protect the logs from tampering. Which architecture should be recommended?
options: A. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs only and set retention to 7 years.

B. Create an organization trail in the management account that delivers logs to a central S3 bucket in a dedicated log archive account. Enable log file integrity validation and apply an S3 bucket policy that denies delete and overwrite actions to all principals except a designated audit role.
C. Enable VPC Flow Logs in every VPC and store them in CloudWatch Logs.
D. Enable AWS CloudTrail in each account separately and store logs in the same account.

question: A company is migrating an application that currently uses a shared database username and password embedded in configuration files. They want to eliminate hard-coded credentials and automatically rotate the password every 30 days. Which AWS service combination is the MOST appropriate?
options: A. Store the password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as a standard parameter and rotate it manually.
B. Create an IAM database user and use IAM authentication only.

C. Use AWS Secrets Manager to store the database credentials, enable automatic rotation with a Lambda rotation function, and update the application to retrieve the secret at runtime using the AWS SDK.
D. Store the password in Amazon S3 and retrieve it at runtime.

question: A public website is hosted on Amazon S3 and fronted by Amazon CloudFront. The company wants to ensure that users can access the content only through CloudFront and never by using the S3 website endpoint or the S3 REST endpoint directly. How should this be enforced?
options: A. Use a security group on the S3 bucket.
B. Enable S3 Block Public Access and remove the bucket policy entirely.
C. Make the S3 bucket public and rely on CloudFront cache behaviors.

D. Create an Origin Access Control (OAC) or Origin Access Identity (OAI) for CloudFront, update the S3 bucket policy to allow access only from the CloudFront service principal / OAI, and deny all other principals.

question: A company needs to allow developers to launch Amazon EC2 instances, but they must only be allowed to launch instances that use encrypted EBS volumes. Which combination of controls should be implemented?
options: A. A network ACL that blocks unencrypted volumes.
B. A security group rule that requires encryption.
C. An S3 bucket policy.
D. An IAM policy that denies ec2:RunInstances when the ebs:Encrypted condition is false, and optionally an AWS Config rule to detect non-compliant instances.

question: An application uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The database contains personal data that must be encrypted at rest. The company also wants to use a customer managed key so they can control key rotation and access. What should the Solutions Architect do?
options: A. Create a new encrypted RDS instance using a customer managed KMS key (CMK), migrate the data, and update the application connection string.
B. Enable encryption with the default AWS managed key and never use a CMK.
C. Use client-side encryption only and leave the RDS instance unencrypted.
D. Enable encryption on an existing unencrypted RDS instance using the modify command.

question: A company has a requirement that all traffic between its Application Load Balancer and the backend EC2 instances must be encrypted in transit. The ALB currently terminates SSL and forwards HTTP to the targets. What change is required?
options: A. Configure the target group to use the HTTPS protocol, install certificates on the EC2 instances (or use ACM certificates where supported), and update the security groups to allow traffic on the HTTPS port.
B. Enable sticky sessions only.
C. Leave the configuration as-is; SSL termination at the ALB is sufficient.
D. Use a Network Load Balancer instead of an Application Load Balancer.

question: A Solutions Architect is reviewing the security of an existing VPC. The VPC has both public and private subnets. The private subnets currently route all outbound traffic (0.0.0.0/0) through a NAT Gateway. The security team wants to ensure that the private instances can reach Amazon S3 without going through the NAT Gateway, to reduce cost and attack surface. What is the BEST solution?
options: A. Create an interface VPC endpoint for S3.
B. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for S3 and add a route in the private subnet route tables that directs S3 traffic to the endpoint.
C. Move the instances to public subnets and assign public IP addresses.
D. Add an internet gateway route to the private subnets.

question: A company wants to detect unusual API activity, such as an IAM user creating multiple access keys or disabling CloudTrail, across all accounts in its AWS Organization. Which service is designed for this continuous threat detection use case?
options: A. Amazon Inspector
B. AWS Trusted Advisor
C. Amazon GuardDuty with a delegated administrator in the organization
D. AWS Config

question: An application needs temporary credentials to access AWS resources. The application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Which mechanism provides the MOST secure short-lived credentials?
options: A. An IAM role attached to the instance via an instance profile; the application retrieves temporary credentials from the instance metadata service (IMDSv2 recommended).
B. IAM user access keys stored in the instance metadata or configuration files.
C. Hard-coded root account credentials.
D. Long-lived access keys rotated every 90 days and stored in environment variables.

question: A company is implementing a zero-trust network model for its VPC. They want to control traffic between application tiers (web, application, database) using identity-aware policies rather than only IP-based rules. Which AWS service can help implement this?
options: A. AWS Verified Access or Amazon VPC Lattice with authentication policies, combined with security groups.
B. Security groups and network ACLs only.
C. AWS WAF on every instance.
D. Only network ACLs with deny rules.

question: A Solutions Architect must ensure that Amazon CloudWatch Logs data is encrypted at rest using a customer managed key. How can this be achieved?
options: A. Store the logs only in Amazon S3 and never use CloudWatch Logs.
B. CloudWatch Logs is always encrypted with an AWS owned key and cannot use a CMK.
C. Encrypt the logs client-side before sending them to CloudWatch.
D. Associate a customer managed KMS key with the CloudWatch Logs log group when it is created or by updating the log group.

question: A company has an Amazon RDS MySQL database that must be accessible only from application servers running in a specific private subnet. Database administrators also need occasional access from a bastion host. How should network access be controlled?
options: A. Place the RDS instance in a public subnet and use a security group that allows 0.0.0.0/0 on port 3306.
B. Place the RDS instance in a private subnet, create a security group for RDS that allows inbound MySQL traffic only from the security groups of the application servers and the bastion host.
C. Use network ACLs only and leave the security group open.
D. Allow inbound traffic from the entire VPC CIDR on the RDS security group.

question: An organization wants to share an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) with another AWS account while ensuring that the AMI cannot be further shared or made public by the receiving account. What is the correct approach?
options: A. Make the AMI public.
B. Share the AMI with the specific AWS account ID and, if needed, use AWS Organizations or License Manager controls; for encrypted AMIs also share the KMS key.
C. Copy the AMI to the other account using the AWS Management Console without any restrictions.
D. Export the AMI to S3 and share the S3 bucket publicly.

question: An organization is subject to strict compliance requirements that mandate encryption of all data in transit and at rest, plus detailed logging of access to sensitive data. They are storing the data in Amazon S3. Which combination of features should be enabled?
options: A. Versioning and MFA Delete only.
B. Client-side encryption only with no server-side encryption.

C. Default encryption with a customer managed KMS key (SSE-KMS), S3 server access logging or CloudTrail data events, and a bucket policy that denies unencrypted uploads (s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption condition).
D. SSE-S3 only and CloudTrail data events for S3.

question: A company runs a three-tier application. The database tier is Amazon RDS. The security team requires that the database credentials used by the application tier are never stored in plain text in the application configuration or environment variables. What is the recommended solution?
options: A. Store the credentials in a plain-text file on the EBS volume of the application servers.
B. Hard-code the credentials in the application source code and re-deploy when they change.

C. Retrieve the credentials at runtime from AWS Secrets Manager (or SSM Parameter Store SecureString) using an IAM role attached to the application instances, and enable automatic rotation if possible.
D. Pass the credentials as command-line arguments when launching the application.

question: A Solutions Architect needs to design a solution that prevents any IAM user or role in a member account from disabling AWS CloudTrail or deleting CloudTrail logs. The accounts are part of an AWS Organization. What is the MOST effective control?
options: A. An IAM policy in each account that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging and s3:DeleteObject on the log bucket.

B. A Service Control Policy (SCP) attached to the organization or organizational units that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, and s3:DeleteObject / s3:PutBucketPolicy on the central log bucket, combined with a central organization trail.
C. A CloudWatch Alarm that notifies when CloudTrail is disabled.
D. Amazon GuardDuty findings only.

question: An application hosted on Amazon EC2 needs to access objects in an S3 bucket. The company wants to ensure that the traffic between the EC2 instances and S3 does not traverse the public internet and does not require a NAT Gateway. The instances are in a private subnet. Which solution should be implemented?
options: A. Use AWS PrivateLink with a Network Load Balancer in front of S3.
B. Create an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 and place it in a public subnet.
C. Assign public IP addresses to the EC2 instances.
D. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 and add the appropriate route to the private subnet route table.

question: A company is building a multi-account environment using AWS Control Tower. They want to ensure that every new account has a baseline set of security controls, including mandatory CloudTrail logging, Config rules, and restricted root user usage. Which feature of Control Tower helps enforce this?
options: A. Only the AWS Organizations management account console.
B. Manual IAM policies applied after account creation.
C. Amazon Macie automatically enabled in every account.
D. Account Factory and Guardrails (both preventive and detective).

question: A financial services company is deploying a new application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application needs to read objects from an Amazon S3 bucket that contains sensitive customer data. The security team requires that no long-term credentials are stored on the instances and that access is limited to the minimum permissions required. What is the most secure way to grant the EC2 instances access to the S3 bucket?
options: A. Create an IAM role with a policy that allows s3:GetObject on the specific bucket, attach the role to an instance profile, and associate the instance profile with the EC2 instances.
B. Create an IAM user with an access key and secret key, store the keys in the application configuration file on each EC2 instance, and use those credentials in the AWS SDK.
C. Create an IAM user, generate access keys, and store the keys in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as SecureString parameters. Retrieve the keys at application startup.
D. Make the S3 bucket public and use unsigned requests from the application.

question: A company is designing a multi-tier web application in a VPC. The application servers run in private subnets and need to download OS patches from the internet. The security team mandates that the servers must not have public IP addresses and that all outbound internet traffic must be controlled and logged. Which solution meets these requirements MOST securely?
options: A. Deploy a NAT Gateway in a public subnet, update the private subnet route tables to point 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT Gateway, and enable VPC Flow Logs.
B. Create a VPC endpoint for every AWS service the servers might need and disable all internet access.
C. Assign Elastic IP addresses to the application servers so they can reach the internet directly.
D. Attach an internet gateway to the VPC and add a route to the internet gateway in the private subnet route tables.

question: A healthcare company must ensure that all objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket are encrypted at rest using keys that the company fully controls and can rotate on demand. The company also wants the ability to disable a key immediately if compromise is suspected. Which solution should a Solutions Architect recommend?
options: A. Enable default encryption on the bucket using SSE-S3 (Amazon S3 managed keys).
B. Require clients to encrypt objects client-side before uploading and store the keys in Amazon DynamoDB.
C. Use SSE-C and manage the encryption keys on the application servers.
D. Enable default encryption on the bucket using SSE-KMS with a customer managed key (CMK) in AWS KMS.

question: A company has multiple AWS accounts under AWS Organizations. The security team wants to prevent any account from creating Amazon S3 buckets that allow public access. They also want a centralized way to detect and remediate any existing public buckets. Which combination of services should be used?
options: A. IAM policies attached to every user denying public access actions.
B. Amazon GuardDuty and Amazon Macie only.
C. AWS CloudTrail and Amazon CloudWatch Alarms only.

D. Service Control Policies (SCPs) to deny s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock with public values, and AWS Config with the s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited and s3-bucket-public-write-prohibited managed rules plus automatic remediation.

question: An application running on Amazon ECS tasks needs to access a database password stored in AWS Secrets Manager. The tasks run in a private subnet with no internet access. How should the architecture be designed so that the tasks can retrieve the secret securely?
options: A. Store the password in an environment variable in the task definition.
B. Use a NAT Gateway and allow the tasks to reach the public Secrets Manager endpoint.

C. Create an interface VPC endpoint for Secrets Manager in the VPC and attach a security group that allows HTTPS from the ECS tasks. Grant the task execution role permission to call secretsmanager:GetSecretValue.
D. Attach an internet gateway to the VPC so the tasks can reach the public Secrets Manager endpoint.

question: An organization is launching a public-facing web application behind an Application Load Balancer. The security team requires that only traffic from the corporate IP ranges can reach the administrative interface, while the main application remains publicly accessible. The administrative interface is hosted on the same ALB using a different path. What is the MOST efficient way to meet this requirement?
options: A. Use AWS WAF on the ALB with an IP set match rule that allows the corporate CIDR ranges only for the administrative path, and allow all other traffic for the main application paths.
B. Create two separate Application Load Balancers — one public and one internal.
C. Place the administrative interface on a separate EC2 instance in a private subnet and use a bastion host.
D. Modify the security group of the ALB to allow traffic only from the corporate IP ranges.

question: A Solutions Architect is designing authentication for a new SaaS application that will be used by employees of many different customer organizations. options: A. AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO) with only the default identity source.
B. Amazon Cognito user pools with SAML identity provider federation.
C. IAM users and groups for every external employee.
D. Amazon Cognito identity pools without user pools.

question: A company stores sensitive documents in Amazon S3. They want to ensure that even the root user of the AWS account cannot permanently delete objects during a defined retention period. Which feature should be enabled?

B. S3 Lifecycle rules that transition objects to Glacier.
C. S3 Versioning only.
D. S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode with a retention period.

question: A web application uses an Application Load Balancer and Amazon EC2 instances. The security team has detected that attackers are attempting SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks. B. AWS Shield Advanced only.
C. Network ACLs with deny rules for all suspicious IP addresses.
D. AWS WAF associated with the Application Load Balancer, using AWS Managed Rules for common threats.

B. Copy the required objects to the development account every night.

question: An application running on Amazon EC2 needs to call Amazon DynamoDB. The security team requires that the traffic never leaves the Amazon network and that no public endpoints are used. How should this be configured?
