D. Use a NAT Gateway and allow the tasks to reach the public Secrets Manager endpoint.

question: An organization is launching a public-facing web application behind an Application Load Balancer. The security team requires that only traffic from the corporate IP ranges can reach the administrative interface, while the main application remains publicly accessible. The administrative interface is hosted on the same ALB using a different path. What is the MOST efficient way to meet this requirement?
options: A. Create two separate Application Load Balancers — one public and one internal.
B. Modify the security group of the ALB to allow traffic only from the corporate IP ranges.
C. Use AWS WAF on the ALB with an IP set match rule that allows the corporate CIDR ranges only for the administrative path, and allow all other traffic for the main application paths.
D. Place the administrative interface on a separate EC2 instance in a private subnet and use a bastion host.

question: A cloud architect is designing authentication for a new SaaS application that will be used by employees of many different customer organizations. Each customer organization already has its own identity provider (IdP) that supports SAML 2.0. The application must allow users to sign in with their existing corporate credentials without creating separate IAM users. Which AWS service should be used?
options: A. AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO) with only the default identity source.
B. Amazon Cognito user pools with SAML identity provider federation.
C. Amazon Cognito identity pools without user pools.
D. IAM users and groups for every external employee.

question: A company stores sensitive documents in Amazon S3. They want to ensure that even the root user of the AWS account cannot permanently delete objects during a defined retention period. Which feature should be enabled?
options: A. S3 Lifecycle rules that transition objects to Glacier.
B. S3 Versioning only.
C. MFA Delete on the bucket.
D. S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode with a retention period.

question: A web application uses an Application Load Balancer and Amazon EC2 instances. The security team has detected that attackers are attempting SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks. Which AWS service should be deployed to protect the application with minimal changes to the existing architecture?
options: A. Network ACLs with deny rules for all suspicious IP addresses.
B. AWS WAF associated with the Application Load Balancer, using AWS Managed Rules for common threats.
C. AWS Shield Advanced only.
D. Amazon Inspector on the EC2 instances.

question: A company runs workloads in multiple AWS accounts. Developers in a development account need temporary access to read objects in a production S3 bucket. The access must be time-limited and auditable. What is the MOST secure approach?
options: A. Make the production S3 bucket public with a bucket policy that allows the development account.
B. Copy the required objects to the development account every night.

C. Create an IAM role in the production account that trusts the development account, attach a least-privilege policy for S3 read access, and allow developers to assume the role using STS. Enable CloudTrail logging.
D. Create a long-lived IAM user in the production account and share the access keys with the developers.

question: An application running on Amazon EC2 needs to call Amazon DynamoDB. The security team requires that the traffic never leaves the Amazon network and that no public endpoints are used. How should this be configured?
options: A. Use an interface VPC endpoint for DynamoDB and place it in a public subnet.
B. Use the public DynamoDB endpoint and rely on HTTPS.
C. Deploy a NAT Gateway and force all traffic through it.
D. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB and update the route table of the subnet where the EC2 instances reside so that DynamoDB traffic is routed through the endpoint.

question: A company wants to enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for any IAM user that attempts to stop or terminate Amazon EC2 instances. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: A. Enable MFA only on the root user.
B. Use Amazon Cognito for all EC2 management.
C. Configure MFA at the VPC level using network ACLs.
D. Attach an IAM policy to all users that includes a condition key aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent set to true for the ec2:StopInstances and ec2:TerminateInstances actions.

question: A Solutions Architect must design a solution that logs all API activity across every AWS account in an organization and retains the logs for 7 years for compliance. The solution must also protect the logs from tampering. Which architecture should be recommended?
options: A. Enable AWS CloudTrail in each account separately and store logs in the same account.

B. Create an organization trail in the management account that delivers logs to a central S3 bucket in a dedicated log archive account. Enable log file integrity validation and apply an S3 bucket policy that denies delete and overwrite actions to all principals except a designated audit role.
C. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs only and set retention to 7 years.
D. Enable VPC Flow Logs in every VPC and store them in CloudWatch Logs.

question: A company is migrating an application that currently uses a shared database username and password embedded in configuration files. They want to eliminate hard-coded credentials and automatically rotate the password every 30 days. Which AWS service combination is the MOST appropriate?
options: A. Use AWS Secrets Manager to store the database credentials, enable automatic rotation with a Lambda rotation function, and update the application to retrieve the secret at runtime using the AWS SDK.
B. Store the password in Amazon S3 and retrieve it at runtime.
C. Create an IAM database user and use IAM authentication only.
D. Store the password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as a standard parameter and rotate it manually.

question: A public website is hosted on Amazon S3 and fronted by Amazon CloudFront. The company wants to ensure that users can access the content only through CloudFront and never by using the S3 website endpoint or the S3 REST endpoint directly. How should this be enforced?
options: A. Create an Origin Access Control (OAC) or Origin Access Identity (OAI) for CloudFront, update the S3 bucket policy to allow access only from the CloudFront service principal / OAI, and deny all other principals.
B. Use a security group on the S3 bucket.
C. Make the S3 bucket public and rely on CloudFront cache behaviors.
D. Enable S3 Block Public Access and remove the bucket policy entirely.

question: A company needs to allow developers to launch Amazon EC2 instances, but they must only be allowed to launch instances that use encrypted EBS volumes. Which combination of controls should be implemented?
options: A. An IAM policy that denies ec2:RunInstances when the ebs:Encrypted condition is false, and optionally an AWS Config rule to detect non-compliant instances.
B. A security group rule that requires encryption.
C. An S3 bucket policy.
D. A network ACL that blocks unencrypted volumes.

question: An application uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The database contains personal data that must be encrypted at rest. The company also wants to use a customer managed key so they can control key rotation and access. What should the Solutions Architect do?
options: A. Enable encryption with the default AWS managed key and never use a CMK.
B. Create a new encrypted RDS instance using a customer managed KMS key (CMK), migrate the data, and update the application connection string.
C. Use client-side encryption only and leave the RDS instance unencrypted.
D. Enable encryption on an existing unencrypted RDS instance using the modify command.

question: An organization has a requirement that all traffic between its Application Load Balancer and the backend EC2 instances must be encrypted in transit. The ALB currently terminates SSL and forwards HTTP to the targets. What change is required?
options: A. Enable sticky sessions only.
B. Use a Network Load Balancer instead of an Application Load Balancer.
C. Leave the configuration as-is; SSL termination at the ALB is sufficient.

D. Configure the target group to use the HTTPS protocol, install certificates on the EC2 instances (or use ACM certificates where supported), and update the security groups to allow traffic on the HTTPS port.

question: A Solutions Architect is reviewing the security of an existing VPC. The VPC has both public and private subnets. The private subnets currently route all outbound traffic (0.0.0.0/0) through a NAT Gateway. The security team wants to ensure that the private instances can reach Amazon S3 without going through the NAT Gateway, to reduce cost and attack surface. What is the BEST solution?
options: A. Create an interface VPC endpoint for S3.
B. Move the instances to public subnets and assign public IP addresses.
C. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for S3 and add a route in the private subnet route tables that directs S3 traffic to the endpoint.
D. Add an internet gateway route to the private subnets.

question: A company wants to detect unusual API activity, such as an IAM user creating multiple access keys or disabling CloudTrail, across all accounts in its AWS Organization. Which service is designed for this continuous threat detection use case?
options: A. Amazon GuardDuty with a delegated administrator in the organization
B. Amazon Inspector
C. AWS Trusted Advisor
D. AWS Config

question: An application needs temporary credentials to access AWS resources. The application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Which mechanism provides the most secure short-lived credentials?
options: A. Hard-coded root account credentials.
B. IAM user access keys stored in the instance metadata or configuration files.
C. An IAM role attached to the instance via an instance profile; the application retrieves temporary credentials from the instance metadata service (IMDSv2 recommended).
D. Long-lived access keys rotated every 90 days and stored in environment variables.

question: A company is implementing a zero-trust network model for its VPC. They want to control traffic between application tiers (web, application, database) using identity-aware policies rather than only IP-based rules. Which AWS service can help implement this?
options: A. Security groups and network ACLs only.
B. Only network ACLs with deny rules.
C. AWS Verified Access or Amazon VPC Lattice with authentication policies, combined with security groups.
D. AWS WAF on every instance.

question: A cloud architect must ensure that Amazon CloudWatch Logs data is encrypted at rest using a customer managed key. How can this be achieved?
options: A. CloudWatch Logs is always encrypted with an AWS owned key and cannot use a CMK.
B. Store the logs only in Amazon S3 and never use CloudWatch Logs.
C. Encrypt the logs client-side before sending them to CloudWatch.
D. Associate a customer managed KMS key with the CloudWatch Logs log group when it is created or by updating the log group.

question: An organization has an Amazon RDS MySQL database that must be accessible only from application servers running in a specific private subnet. Database administrators also need occasional access from a bastion host. How should network access be controlled?
options: A. Allow inbound traffic from the entire VPC CIDR on the RDS security group.
B. Place the RDS instance in a private subnet, create a security group for RDS that allows inbound MySQL traffic only from the security groups of the application servers and the bastion host.
C. Place the RDS instance in a public subnet and use a security group that allows 0.0.0.0/0 on port 3306.
D. Use network ACLs only and leave the security group open.

question: An organization wants to share an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) with another AWS account while ensuring that the AMI cannot be further shared or made public by the receiving account. What is the correct approach?
options: A. Make the AMI public.
B. Export the AMI to S3 and share the S3 bucket publicly.
C. Share the AMI with the specific AWS account ID and, if needed, use AWS Organizations or License Manager controls; for encrypted AMIs also share the KMS key.
D. Copy the AMI to the other account using the AWS Management Console without any restrictions.

question: An organization is subject to strict compliance requirements that mandate encryption of all data in transit and at rest, plus detailed logging of access to sensitive data. They are storing the data in Amazon S3. Which combination of features should be enabled?
options: A. Client-side encryption only with no server-side encryption.
B. Versioning and MFA Delete only.
C. SSE-S3 only and CloudTrail data events for S3.

D. Default encryption with a customer managed KMS key (SSE-KMS), S3 server access logging or CloudTrail data events, and a bucket policy that denies unencrypted uploads (s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption condition).

question: An organization runs a three-tier application. The database tier is Amazon RDS. The security team requires that the database credentials used by the application tier are never stored in plain text in the application configuration or environment variables. What is the recommended solution?
options: A. Store the credentials in a plain-text file on the EBS volume of the application servers.
B. Hard-code the credentials in the application source code and re-deploy when they change.

C. Retrieve the credentials at runtime from AWS Secrets Manager (or SSM Parameter Store SecureString) using an IAM role attached to the application instances, and enable automatic rotation if possible.
D. Pass the credentials as command-line arguments when launching the application.

question: A cloud architect needs to design a solution that prevents any IAM user or role in a member account from disabling AWS CloudTrail or deleting CloudTrail logs. The accounts are part of an AWS Organization. What is the MOST effective control?
options: A. An IAM policy in each account that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging and s3:DeleteObject on the log bucket.

D. Amazon GuardDuty findings only.

question: An application hosted on Amazon EC2 needs to access objects in an S3 bucket. The company wants to ensure that the traffic between the EC2 instances and S3 does not traverse the public internet and does not require a NAT Gateway. The instances are in a private subnet. Which solution should be implemented?
options: A. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 and add the appropriate route to the private subnet route table.
B. Create an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 and place it in a public subnet.
C. Use AWS PrivateLink with a Network Load Balancer in front of S3.
D. Assign public IP addresses to the EC2 instances.

question: An organization is building a multi-account environment using AWS Control Tower. C. Only the AWS Organizations management account console.
D. Amazon Macie automatically enabled in every account.

question: A financial services company is deploying a new application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application needs to read objects from an Amazon S3 bucket that contains sensitive customer data. question: A healthcare company must ensure that all objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket are encrypted at rest using keys that the company fully controls and can rotate on demand. question: A company has multiple AWS accounts under AWS Organizations. The security team wants to prevent any account from creating Amazon S3 buckets that allow public access. B. AWS CloudTrail and Amazon CloudWatch Alarms only.

D. IAM policies attached to every user denying public access actions.

question: An application running on Amazon ECS tasks needs to access a database password stored in AWS Secrets Manager. The tasks run in a private subnet with no internet access. How should the architecture be designed so that the tasks can retrieve the secret securely?

options: A. Manual IAM policies applied after account creation.
B. Account Factory and Guardrails (both preventive and detective).
C. Amazon Macie automatically enabled in every account.
D. Only the AWS Organizations management account console.

question: A financial services company is deploying a new application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application needs to read objects from an Amazon S3 bucket that contains sensitive customer data. The security team requires that no long-term credentials are stored on the instances and that access is limited to the minimum permissions required. What is the MOST secure way to grant the EC2 instances access to the S3 bucket?
options: A. Create an IAM user, generate access keys, and store the keys in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as SecureString parameters. Retrieve the keys at application startup.
B. Create an IAM user with an access key and secret key, store the keys in the application configuration file on each EC2 instance, and use those credentials in the AWS SDK.
C. Make the S3 bucket public and use unsigned requests from the application.
D. Create an IAM role with a policy that allows s3:GetObject on the specific bucket, attach the role to an instance profile, and associate the instance profile with the EC2 instances.

question: A company is designing a multi-tier web application in a VPC. The application servers run in private subnets and need to download OS patches from the internet. The security team mandates that the servers must not have public IP addresses and that all outbound internet traffic must be controlled and logged. Which solution meets these requirements MOST securely?
options: A. Create a VPC endpoint for every AWS service the servers might need and disable all internet access.
B. Deploy a NAT Gateway in a public subnet, update the private subnet route tables to point 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT Gateway, and enable VPC Flow Logs.
C. Assign Elastic IP addresses to the application servers so they can reach the internet directly.
D. Attach an internet gateway to the VPC and add a route to the internet gateway in the private subnet route tables.

question: A healthcare company must ensure that all objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket are encrypted at rest using keys that the company fully controls and can rotate on demand. The company also wants the ability to disable a key immediately if compromise is suspected. Which solution should a Solutions Architect recommend?
options: A. Enable default encryption on the bucket using SSE-KMS with a customer managed key (CMK) in AWS KMS.
B. Use SSE-C and manage the encryption keys on the application servers.
C. Require clients to encrypt objects client-side before uploading and store the keys in Amazon DynamoDB.
D. Enable default encryption on the bucket using SSE-S3 (Amazon S3 managed keys).

question: An organization has multiple AWS accounts under AWS Organizations. The security team wants to prevent any account from creating Amazon S3 buckets that allow public access. They also want a centralized way to detect and remediate any existing public buckets. Which combination of services should be used?
options: A. Service Control Policies (SCPs) to deny s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock with public values, and AWS Config with the s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited and s3-bucket-public-write-prohibited managed rules plus automatic remediation.
B. AWS CloudTrail and Amazon CloudWatch Alarms only.
C. IAM policies attached to every user denying public access actions.
D. Amazon GuardDuty and Amazon Macie only.

question: An application running on Amazon ECS tasks needs to access a database password stored in AWS Secrets Manager. The tasks run in a private subnet with no internet access. How should the architecture be designed so that the tasks can retrieve the secret securely?
options: A. Create an interface VPC endpoint for Secrets Manager in the VPC and attach a security group that allows HTTPS from the ECS tasks. Grant the task execution role permission to call secretsmanager:GetSecretValue.
B. Attach an internet gateway to the VPC so the tasks can reach the public Secrets Manager endpoint.
C. Store the password in an environment variable in the task definition.
D. Use a NAT Gateway and allow the tasks to reach the public Secrets Manager endpoint.

question: A company is launching a public-facing web application behind an Application Load Balancer. The security team requires that only traffic from the corporate IP ranges can reach the administrative interface, while the main application remains publicly accessible. The administrative interface is hosted on the same ALB using a different path. What is the MOST efficient way to meet this requirement?
options: A. Place the administrative interface on a separate EC2 instance in a private subnet and use a bastion host.
B. Create two separate Application Load Balancers — one public and one internal.
C. Modify the security group of the ALB to allow traffic only from the corporate IP ranges.
D. Use AWS WAF on the ALB with an IP set match rule that allows the corporate CIDR ranges only for the administrative path, and allow all other traffic for the main application paths.

question: A Solutions Architect is designing authentication for a new SaaS application that will be used by employees of many different customer organizations. Each customer organization already has its own identity provider (IdP) that supports SAML 2.0. The application must allow users to sign in with their existing corporate credentials without creating separate IAM users. Which AWS service should be used?
options: A. Amazon Cognito identity pools without user pools.
B. AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO) with only the default identity source.
C. IAM users and groups for every external employee.
D. Amazon Cognito user pools with SAML identity provider federation.

question: An organization stores sensitive documents in Amazon S3. They want to ensure that even the root user of the AWS account cannot permanently delete objects during a defined retention period. Which feature should be enabled?
options: A. S3 Versioning only.
B. S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode with a retention period.
C. S3 Lifecycle rules that transition objects to Glacier.
D. MFA Delete on the bucket.

question: A web application uses an Application Load Balancer and Amazon EC2 instances. The security team has detected that attackers are attempting SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks. Which AWS service should be deployed to protect the application with minimal changes to the existing architecture?
options: A. Network ACLs with deny rules for all suspicious IP addresses.
B. Amazon Inspector on the EC2 instances.
C. AWS Shield Advanced only.
D. AWS WAF associated with the Application Load Balancer, using AWS Managed Rules for common threats.

question: A company runs workloads in multiple AWS accounts. Developers in a development account need temporary access to read objects in a production S3 bucket. The access must be time-limited and auditable. What is the MOST secure approach?
options: A. Create a long-lived IAM user in the production account and share the access keys with the developers.
B. Make the production S3 bucket public with a bucket policy that allows the development account.

C. Create an IAM role in the production account that trusts the development account, attach a least-privilege policy for S3 read access, and allow developers to assume the role using STS. Enable CloudTrail logging.
D. Copy the required objects to the development account every night.

question: An application running on Amazon EC2 needs to call Amazon DynamoDB. The security team requires that the traffic never leaves the Amazon network and that no public endpoints are used. How should this be configured?
options: A. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB and update the route table of the subnet where the EC2 instances reside so that DynamoDB traffic is routed through the endpoint.
B. Use an interface VPC endpoint for DynamoDB and place it in a public subnet.
C. Use the public DynamoDB endpoint and rely on HTTPS.
D. Deploy a NAT Gateway and force all traffic through it.

question: A company wants to enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for any IAM user that attempts to stop or terminate Amazon EC2 instances. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: A. Enable MFA only on the root user.
B. Configure MFA at the VPC level using network ACLs.
C. Use Amazon Cognito for all EC2 management.
D. Attach an IAM policy to all users that includes a condition key aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent set to true for the ec2:StopInstances and ec2:TerminateInstances actions.

question: A cloud architect must design a solution that logs all API activity across every AWS account in an organization and retains the logs for 7 years for compliance. The solution must also protect the logs from tampering. Which architecture should be recommended?
options: A. Enable AWS CloudTrail in each account separately and store logs in the same account.
B. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs only and set retention to 7 years.
C. Enable VPC Flow Logs in every VPC and store them in CloudWatch Logs.

D. Create an organization trail in the management account that delivers logs to a central S3 bucket in a dedicated log archive account. Enable log file integrity validation and apply an S3 bucket policy that denies delete and overwrite actions to all principals except a designated audit role.

question: A company is migrating an application that currently uses a shared database username and password embedded in configuration files. They want to eliminate hard-coded credentials and automatically rotate the password every 30 days. Which AWS service combination is the MOST appropriate?
options: A. Store the password in Amazon S3 and retrieve it at runtime.
B. Store the password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as a standard parameter and rotate it manually.
C. Create an IAM database user and use IAM authentication only.

D. Use AWS Secrets Manager to store the database credentials, enable automatic rotation with a Lambda rotation function, and update the application to retrieve the secret at runtime using the AWS SDK.

question: A public website is hosted on Amazon S3 and fronted by Amazon CloudFront. The company wants to ensure that users can access the content only through CloudFront and never by using the S3 website endpoint or the S3 REST endpoint directly. How should this be enforced?
options: A. Make the S3 bucket public and rely on CloudFront cache behaviors.

B. Create an Origin Access Control (OAC) or Origin Access Identity (OAI) for CloudFront, update the S3 bucket policy to allow access only from the CloudFront service principal / OAI, and deny all other principals.
C. Use a security group on the S3 bucket.
D. Enable S3 Block Public Access and remove the bucket policy entirely.

question: A company needs to allow developers to launch Amazon EC2 instances, but they must only be allowed to launch instances that use encrypted EBS volumes. Which combination of controls should be implemented?
options: A. An IAM policy that denies ec2:RunInstances when the ebs:Encrypted condition is false, and optionally an AWS Config rule to detect non-compliant instances.
B. A network ACL that blocks unencrypted volumes.
C. A security group rule that requires encryption.
D. An S3 bucket policy.

question: An application uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The database contains personal data that must be encrypted at rest. The company also wants to use a customer managed key so they can control key rotation and access. What should the Solutions Architect do?
options: A. Enable encryption with the default AWS managed key and never use a CMK.
B. Enable encryption on an existing unencrypted RDS instance using the modify command.
C. Use client-side encryption only and leave the RDS instance unencrypted.
D. Create a new encrypted RDS instance using a customer managed KMS key (CMK), migrate the data, and update the application connection string.

question: A company has a requirement that all traffic between its Application Load Balancer and the backend EC2 instances must be encrypted in transit. The ALB currently terminates SSL and forwards HTTP to the targets. What change is required?
options: A. Leave the configuration as-is; SSL termination at the ALB is sufficient.

B. Configure the target group to use the HTTPS protocol, install certificates on the EC2 instances (or use ACM certificates where supported), and update the security groups to allow traffic on the HTTPS port.
C. Enable sticky sessions only.
D. Use a Network Load Balancer instead of an Application Load Balancer.

question: A Solutions Architect is reviewing the security of an existing VPC. The VPC has both public and private subnets. The private subnets currently route all outbound traffic (0.0.0.0/0) through a NAT Gateway. The security team wants to ensure that the private instances can reach Amazon S3 without going through the NAT Gateway, to reduce cost and attack surface. What is the BEST solution?
options: A. Move the instances to public subnets and assign public IP addresses.
B. Add an internet gateway route to the private subnets.
C. Create an interface VPC endpoint for S3.
D. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for S3 and add a route in the private subnet route tables that directs S3 traffic to the endpoint.

question: A company wants to detect unusual API activity, such as an IAM user creating multiple access keys or disabling CloudTrail, across all accounts in its AWS Organization. Which service is designed for this continuous threat detection use case?
options: A. Amazon GuardDuty with a delegated administrator in the organization
B. Amazon Inspector
C. AWS Config
D. AWS Trusted Advisor

question: An application needs temporary credentials to access AWS resources. The application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Which mechanism provides the most secure short-lived credentials?
options: A. IAM user access keys stored in the instance metadata or configuration files.
B. Long-lived access keys rotated every 90 days and stored in environment variables.
C. An IAM role attached to the instance via an instance profile; the application retrieves temporary credentials from the instance metadata service (IMDSv2 recommended).
D. Hard-coded root account credentials.

question: An organization is implementing a zero-trust network model for its VPC. They want to control traffic between application tiers (web, application, database) using identity-aware policies rather than only IP-based rules. Which AWS service can help implement this?
options: A. Only network ACLs with deny rules.
B. AWS WAF on every instance.
C. Security groups and network ACLs only.
D. AWS Verified Access or Amazon VPC Lattice with authentication policies, combined with security groups.

question: A Solutions Architect must ensure that Amazon CloudWatch Logs data is encrypted at rest using a customer managed key. How can this be achieved?
options: A. Associate a customer managed KMS key with the CloudWatch Logs log group when it is created or by updating the log group.
B. CloudWatch Logs is always encrypted with an AWS owned key and cannot use a CMK.
C. Encrypt the logs client-side before sending them to CloudWatch.
D. Store the logs only in Amazon S3 and never use CloudWatch Logs.

question: A company has an Amazon RDS MySQL database that must be accessible only from application servers running in a specific private subnet. Database administrators also need occasional access from a bastion host. How should network access be controlled?
options: A. Place the RDS instance in a private subnet, create a security group for RDS that allows inbound MySQL traffic only from the security groups of the application servers and the bastion host.
B. Use network ACLs only and leave the security group open.
C. Allow inbound traffic from the entire VPC CIDR on the RDS security group.
D. Place the RDS instance in a public subnet and use a security group that allows 0.0.0.0/0 on port 3306.

question: A company wants to share an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) with another AWS account while ensuring that the AMI cannot be further shared or made public by the receiving account. What is the correct approach?
options: A. Share the AMI with the specific AWS account ID and, if needed, use AWS Organizations or License Manager controls; for encrypted AMIs also share the KMS key.
B. Export the AMI to S3 and share the S3 bucket publicly.
C. Make the AMI public.
D. Copy the AMI to the other account using the AWS Management Console without any restrictions.

question: An organization is subject to strict compliance requirements that mandate encryption of all data in transit and at rest, plus detailed logging of access to sensitive data. They are storing the data in Amazon S3. Which combination of features should be enabled?
options: A. Client-side encryption only with no server-side encryption.
B. Versioning and MFA Delete only.
C. SSE-S3 only and CloudTrail data events for S3.

D. Default encryption with a customer managed KMS key (SSE-KMS), S3 server access logging or CloudTrail data events, and a bucket policy that denies unencrypted uploads (s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption condition).

question: A company runs a three-tier application. The database tier is Amazon RDS. The security team requires that the database credentials used by the application tier are never stored in plain text in the application configuration or environment variables. What is the recommended solution?
options: A. Store the credentials in a plain-text file on the EBS volume of the application servers.

B. Retrieve the credentials at runtime from AWS Secrets Manager (or SSM Parameter Store SecureString) using an IAM role attached to the application instances, and enable automatic rotation if possible.
C. Pass the credentials as command-line arguments when launching the application.
D. Hard-code the credentials in the application source code and re-deploy when they change.

question: A Solutions Architect needs to design a solution that prevents any IAM user or role in a member account from disabling AWS CloudTrail or deleting CloudTrail logs. The accounts are part of an AWS Organization. What is the MOST effective control?
options: A. An IAM policy in each account that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging and s3:DeleteObject on the log bucket.
B. A CloudWatch Alarm that notifies when CloudTrail is disabled.
C. Amazon GuardDuty findings only.

D. A Service Control Policy (SCP) attached to the organization or organizational units that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, and s3:DeleteObject / s3:PutBucketPolicy on the central log bucket, combined with a central organization trail.

question: An application hosted on Amazon EC2 needs to access objects in an S3 bucket. The company wants to ensure that the traffic between the EC2 instances and S3 does not traverse the public internet and does not require a NAT Gateway. The instances are in a private subnet. Which solution should be implemented?
options: A. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 and add the appropriate route to the private subnet route table.
B. Assign public IP addresses to the EC2 instances.
C. Use AWS PrivateLink with a Network Load Balancer in front of S3.
D. Create an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 and place it in a public subnet.

question: An organization is building a multi-account environment using AWS Control Tower. They want to ensure that every new account has a baseline set of security controls, including mandatory CloudTrail logging, Config rules, and restricted root user usage. Which feature of Control Tower helps enforce this?
options: A. Manual IAM policies applied after account creation.
B. Only the AWS Organizations management account console.
C. Amazon Macie automatically enabled in every account.
D. Account Factory and Guardrails (both preventive and detective).

question: An organization runs a critical web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application currently runs in a single Availability Zone. The business requires that the application remain available even if an entire Availability Zone fails. What changes should the Solutions Architect make?
options: A. Move the application to AWS Lambda to eliminate the need for Availability Zones.
B. Create an Auto Scaling group that spans at least two Availability Zones, register the instances with the Application Load Balancer, and ensure the ALB is configured for multiple AZs.
C. Add a second Application Load Balancer in the same AZ.
D. Increase the size of the EC2 instances in the existing AZ so they can handle the full load.

question: An e-commerce application processes orders asynchronously. During peak sales events the order volume can increase by 20x. The current architecture has the web tier writing orders directly to a relational database, which becomes a bottleneck and causes timeouts. How should the architecture be redesigned for better resilience and scalability?
options: A. Increase the size of the database instance and add more read replicas.

B. Place an Amazon SQS queue between the web tier and the order-processing workers. The web tier enqueues orders; worker instances (or Lambda functions) poll the queue and write to the database. Use an Auto Scaling group for the workers based on queue depth.
C. Add more web servers and keep the synchronous database writes.
D. Replace the relational database with a single Amazon DynamoDB table and keep synchronous writes from the web tier.

question: A company uses Amazon RDS for MySQL as the primary database for a production application. The Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is 5 minutes and the Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is near zero. Which configuration BEST meets these requirements?
options: A. Database running on a single EC2 instance with EBS snapshots every hour.
B. Single-AZ RDS instance with automated backups retained for 7 days.
C. Multi-AZ RDS deployment (synchronous standby in a second AZ) with automated backups.
D. Single-AZ RDS with a read replica in another Region and manual promotion.

question: A global company needs its application to remain available even if an entire AWS Region becomes unavailable. The application consists of a web tier, an application tier, and a database. The RTO is 1 hour. Which disaster recovery strategy is the MOST cost-effective while still meeting the RTO?
options: A. Backup and restore: store daily backups in S3 and rebuild everything from scratch in a new Region when a disaster occurs.
B. Warm standby with a full-scale duplicate environment running in the second Region at all times.
C. Active-active multi-Region deployment with continuous traffic to both Regions.

D. Pilot light: keep a minimal version of the core infrastructure (database replica, AMI, basic networking) running in a second Region and scale out when needed. Use Route 53 health checks and failover routing.

question: A microservices application uses Amazon SQS for inter-service communication. Occasionally a message cannot be processed successfully even after several retries, and the team wants to isolate those messages for later analysis without blocking the main queue. What should be configured?
options: A. Use Amazon SNS instead of SQS.
B. Delete messages that fail processing immediately.
C. Increase the visibility timeout to the maximum value.
D. Configure a dead-letter queue (DLQ) on the main SQS queue and set a maximum receive count. After the threshold is reached, messages are automatically moved to the DLQ.

question: A company hosts a static website on Amazon S3. They want the website to remain available even if the primary S3 bucket or the Region becomes unavailable. Which architecture provides the highest availability?
options: A. Two S3 buckets in different Regions, with Amazon CloudFront configured with origin failover (primary and secondary origins), and Route 53 health checks if needed.
B. Hosting the website on a single EC2 instance.
C. A single S3 bucket with versioning enabled.
D. An S3 bucket behind an Application Load Balancer.

question: An application runs on Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type. The service must be able to survive the failure of an Availability Zone. How should the service be configured?
options: A. Configure the ECS service to use multiple subnets across at least two Availability Zones and set the desired count high enough that tasks can be redistributed if one AZ fails. Use a load balancer that spans the same AZs.
B. Disable cross-zone load balancing.
C. Deploy the service in a single AZ and increase the number of tasks.
D. Use only the EC2 launch type with a single large instance.

question: A company has an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. They need to scale read capacity for reporting queries without impacting the primary transactional workload, and they also need automatic failover if the primary instance fails. Which Aurora configuration should be used?
options: A. Standard RDS MySQL with a single read replica in the same AZ.
B. An Aurora DB cluster with a primary instance and at least one Aurora Replica. Use the cluster endpoint for writes and the reader endpoint for reads. Multi-AZ is inherent in the storage layer.
C. A single Aurora instance with no replicas.
D. Two independent Aurora clusters with application-level failover logic only.

question: A Solutions Architect is designing a system that processes financial transactions. The system must not lose any messages even if a processing component fails, and messages must be processed in the order they were received for each customer. Which Amazon SQS configuration is required?
options: A. Standard queue with long polling.
B. FIFO queue with content-based deduplication (or explicit deduplication IDs) and a message group ID based on the customer identifier.
C. Amazon SNS topic with multiple SQS subscribers.
D. Standard queue with a dead-letter queue only.

question: An organization uses Amazon Route 53 to route traffic to an application hosted in two AWS Regions. They want traffic to be directed to the Region with the lowest latency for each user, but if a Region becomes unhealthy, all traffic should fail over to the healthy Region. Which routing policy and feature combination should be used?
options: A. Weighted routing with equal weights and no health checks.
B. Geolocation routing only.
C. Latency-based routing with health checks associated with each record set. Route 53 will stop routing to an unhealthy Region.
D. Simple routing with no health checks.

question: An Auto Scaling group is configured to maintain a minimum of 4 instances across two Availability Zones. During a routine scale-out, some new instances fail the Application Load Balancer health checks because the application takes 3 minutes to start. What should the Solutions Architect configure to prevent the Auto Scaling group from terminating these instances prematurely?
options: A. Disable ELB health checks and use only EC2 status checks.

B. Set an appropriate health check grace period (for example 180–300 seconds) on the Auto Scaling group so that newly launched instances are not considered unhealthy until the application has finished starting.
C. Increase the desired capacity to 10.
D. Reduce the minimum instance count to 2.

question: An organization needs a shared file system that can be mounted concurrently by hundreds of EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones and must remain available if one AZ fails. Which service meets this requirement?
options: A. Amazon EFS (Elastic File System) configured with mount targets in multiple AZs.
B. Amazon EBS Multi-Attach volumes.
C. Amazon S3 mounted via s3fs on each instance.
D. Instance store volumes shared via NFS from one instance.

question: A production application uses Amazon DynamoDB. The team wants the table to remain available even if an entire AWS Region becomes unavailable, with a recovery point objective of a few seconds. Which DynamoDB feature should be enabled?
options: A. DynamoDB global tables with replicas in at least two Regions.
B. DynamoDB Streams without any cross-Region replication.
C. Point-in-time recovery (PITR) only.
D. On-Demand capacity mode only.

question: A company is designing a serverless application using AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, and Amazon DynamoDB. They want the application to degrade gracefully if the DynamoDB table becomes throttled or temporarily unavailable. Which pattern improves resilience?
options: A. Make all Lambda functions synchronous and fail immediately on any DynamoDB error.
B. Increase the Lambda timeout to 15 minutes and never retry.

C. Implement retries with exponential backoff and jitter in the Lambda code (or use the AWS SDK built-in retry logic), consider a circuit breaker, and optionally use an SQS queue as a buffer for write operations.
D. Replace DynamoDB with a single EC2-hosted database.

question: An application currently runs on a single large EC2 instance. The business wants to improve availability and the ability to scale without downtime. Which architecture change provides the greatest improvement in resilience?
options: A. Migrate to an Auto Scaling group spanning multiple Availability Zones behind a load balancer, and move session state to an external store such as DynamoDB or ElastiCache if the application is stateful.
B. Move the application to a single Lambda function.
C. Add a second instance in the same AZ and use DNS round-robin.
D. Increase the instance size to the largest available type.

question: A company uses Amazon RDS and wants to reduce the recovery time in case of a failure of the primary instance. They also want to offload read-only reporting queries. Which combination should be implemented?
options: A. Amazon Aurora Serverless only, without any replicas.
B. Two independent single-AZ RDS instances with application-level replication.
C. Single-AZ RDS with one read replica in the same AZ.
D. Multi-AZ RDS deployment for automatic failover, plus one or more read replicas (in the same or different AZs/Regions) for reporting workloads.

question: A Solutions Architect must design a solution for processing images uploaded by users. The processing can take several minutes and must not be lost if a worker fails. The system should automatically scale based on the number of pending images. Which architecture is MOST resilient and scalable?
options: A. Use a single long-running EC2 instance that polls an S3 bucket every minute.

B. Users upload images to Amazon S3. S3 event notifications send a message to an SQS queue. An Auto Scaling group of EC2 workers (or Lambda functions) polls the queue, processes the images, and writes results back to S3. Failed messages go to a dead-letter queue.
C. Users upload images directly to an EC2 instance that processes them synchronously.
D. Users upload images to an EBS volume attached to a single EC2 instance.

question: A company has a multi-tier application with a web tier, application tier, and database tier. They want to ensure that a failure in the web tier does not cascade and take down the entire system. Which design principle should be applied?
options: A. Placing all tiers on the same EC2 instance.
B. Tight coupling between all tiers using synchronous calls with no timeouts.
C. Loose coupling using message queues (SQS) or pub/sub (SNS/EventBridge) between tiers, health checks, circuit breakers, and independent Auto Scaling for each tier.
D. Using a single shared database connection pool without isolation.

question: An Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group is used for a stateful application that stores session data on the local disk. When instances are terminated during scale-in, users lose their sessions. How can this be resolved while still using Auto Scaling?
options: A. Increase the health check grace period to 1 hour.
B. Move session state to an external shared store such as Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon ElastiCache, or a shared EFS file system, and configure the Auto Scaling group to use ELB health checks.
C. Disable scale-in completely.
D. Use only Spot Instances so that interruptions are expected.

question: An organization needs to ensure that its Amazon Aurora database can survive the failure of an entire Availability Zone with minimal downtime. What is the recommended configuration?
options: A. A single Aurora instance in one AZ.
B. Using Amazon RDS for MySQL with a single Multi-AZ standby only, without Aurora.
C. Two separate Aurora clusters in the same AZ with manual failover.
D. An Aurora cluster with the primary instance and at least one replica placed in different Availability Zones. Aurora storage is already replicated across three AZs.

question: A global application uses Amazon CloudFront. The origin is an Application Load Balancer in a single Region. The company wants the application to remain available if that Region fails. Which approach provides origin failover capability?
options: A. Use only a single origin and rely on CloudFront edge caching.
B. Create a second ALB in another Region and configure CloudFront origin groups with a primary and secondary origin, plus health checks.
C. Increase the CloudFront cache TTL to the maximum value.
D. Move the origin to Amazon S3 only.

question: An organization runs batch jobs on Amazon EC2 that can take several hours to complete. Occasionally an instance fails midway through a job. The company wants failed jobs to be retried automatically without manual intervention. Which service combination provides a resilient solution?
options: A. Amazon ECS tasks without any retry logic.

B. AWS Batch with a managed compute environment, job queues, and job definitions that specify retry strategies. Alternatively, Step Functions with error handling and retries, or an SQS-based worker pattern with a DLQ.
C. A single EC2 instance that runs a cron job.
D. AWS Lambda with a 15-minute timeout and no retry configuration.

question: A Solutions Architect is designing the networking for a highly available application. The application requires low-latency communication between instances. Which placement strategy should be used carefully, and what is the trade-off?
options: A. No placement group is ever needed.
B. Partition placement group guarantees the lowest possible latency.
C. Spread placement group only — always the best for both latency and availability.
D. Cluster placement group — provides the lowest latency but concentrates instances in a single AZ, reducing availability if that AZ fails.

question: An application uses Amazon SQS Standard queues. Under rare conditions the same message is delivered more than once. The application must handle this without creating duplicate records in the database. What is the recommended approach?
options: A. Reduce the visibility timeout to 1 second.
B. Switch to a FIFO queue only and never use Standard queues.
C. Disable long polling.
D. Design the application to be idempotent — for example by using a unique transaction ID as a primary key or by checking whether the work has already been performed before writing to the database.

question: A company has a requirement that their critical application must have an RPO of 5 minutes and an RTO of 30 minutes in the event of a Regional failure. Which disaster recovery strategy is appropriate and cost-effective?
options: A. Active-active with full capacity in both Regions at all times (highest cost).

B. Warm standby: a scaled-down but fully functional environment running in a second Region, with continuous or frequent data replication (for example Aurora global database or DynamoDB global tables). Scale up and fail over using Route 53 when needed.
C. Backup and restore with daily backups only.
D. Pilot light with only backups and no running infrastructure.

question: An application uses Amazon SQS Standard queues. Under rare conditions the same message is delivered more than once. The application must handle this without creating duplicate records in the database. What is the recommended approach?

C. Switch to a FIFO queue only and never use Standard queues.
D. Reduce the visibility timeout to 1 second.

question: A company has a requirement that their critical application must have an RPO of 5 minutes and an RTO of 30 minutes in the event of a Regional failure. Which disaster recovery strategy is appropriate and cost-effective?
options: A. Active-active with full capacity in both Regions at all times (highest cost).
B. Pilot light with only backups and no running infrastructure.

C. Warm standby: a scaled-down but fully functional environment running in a second Region, with continuous or frequent data replication (for example Aurora global database or DynamoDB global tables). Scale up and fail over using Route 53 when needed.
D. Backup and restore with daily backups only.

question: An Auto Scaling group is used with an Application Load Balancer. The company observes that when an instance fails its health check, it continues to receive traffic for a short period. How can this be improved?
options: A. Increase the desired capacity permanently.
B. Disable health checks on the target group.

C. Ensure the target group health check is correctly configured (path, interval, healthy/unhealthy thresholds) and that the Auto Scaling group uses ELB health checks so that unhealthy instances are replaced. Connection draining (deregistration delay) can be tuned as needed.
D. Use only EC2 status checks and ignore ELB health checks.

question: An organization wants to protect its application from the failure of a single EC2 instance and from the failure of an entire Availability Zone. The application is currently deployed on two instances in one AZ. What is the minimum change required?
options: A. Add two more instances in the same AZ.
B. Redeploy the instances across at least two Availability Zones and place them behind a load balancer that is also multi-AZ. Use an Auto Scaling group to maintain the desired count.
C. Move both instances to a different AZ.
D. Replace the instances with a single larger instance.

question: A serverless application uses Amazon EventBridge to route events to multiple Lambda functions. Occasionally one of the downstream functions fails. The team wants failed events to be captured for later analysis without losing them. What should be configured?
options: A. Use only synchronous invocations and ignore errors.
B. Disable the EventBridge rule when errors occur.
C. Configure a dead-letter queue (SQS or SNS) on the EventBridge rule or on the Lambda function for asynchronous invocations.
D. Increase the Lambda concurrency limit.

question: A company runs a legacy application that must keep state on the local file system. They want to improve availability by using multiple instances behind a load balancer, but the local state is a problem. Which AWS storage service can provide a shared file system that multiple EC2 instances can mount concurrently?
options: A. Instance store volumes.
B. Amazon EFS or Amazon FSx for Windows File Server / FSx for NetApp ONTAP, depending on the OS and protocol requirements.
C. Amazon EBS volumes (standard single-attach).
D. Amazon S3 with the AWS SDK only.

question: A cloud architect is designing a multi-Region active-passive architecture. The database is Amazon Aurora. Which Aurora feature provides the lowest RPO for cross-Region replication?
options: A. Standard Aurora read replicas in another Region with asynchronous binlog replication.

C. Aurora Global Database, which uses dedicated replication infrastructure with typical lag under 1 second.

question: An organization runs a critical web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application currently runs in a single Availability Zone. B. Move the application to AWS Lambda to eliminate the need for Availability Zones.
C. Increase the size of the EC2 instances in the existing AZ so they can handle the full load.
D. Create an Auto Scaling group that spans at least two Availability Zones, register the instances with the Application Load Balancer, and ensure the ALB is configured for multiple AZs.

question: An e-commerce application processes orders asynchronously. During peak sales events the order volume can increase by 20x. The current architecture has the web tier writing orders directly to a relational database, which becomes a bottleneck and causes timeouts. How should the architecture be redesigned for better resilience and scalability?
options: A. Place an Amazon SQS queue between the web tier and the order-processing workers. The web tier enqueues orders; worker instances (or Lambda functions) poll the queue and write to the database. Use an Auto Scaling group for the workers based on queue depth.
B. Replace the relational database with a single Amazon DynamoDB table and keep synchronous writes from the web tier.
C. Increase the size of the database instance and add more read replicas.
D. Add more web servers and keep the synchronous database writes.

question: A company uses Amazon RDS for MySQL as the primary database for a production application. The Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is 5 minutes and the Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is near zero. Which configuration BEST meets these requirements?
options: A. Database running on a single EC2 instance with EBS snapshots every hour.
B. Single-AZ RDS instance with automated backups retained for 7 days.
C. Multi-AZ RDS deployment (synchronous standby in a second AZ) with automated backups.
D. Single-AZ RDS with a read replica in another Region and manual promotion.

question: A global company needs its application to remain available even if an entire AWS Region becomes unavailable. The application consists of a web tier, an application tier, and a database. The RTO is 1 hour. Which disaster recovery strategy is the most cost-effective while still meeting the RTO?
options: A. Active-active multi-Region deployment with continuous traffic to both Regions.

B. Pilot light: keep a minimal version of the core infrastructure (database replica, AMI, basic networking) running in a second Region and scale out when needed. Use Route 53 health checks and failover routing.
C. Warm standby with a full-scale duplicate environment running in the second Region at all times.
D. Backup and restore: store daily backups in S3 and rebuild everything from scratch in a new Region when a disaster occurs.

question: A microservices application uses Amazon SQS for inter-service communication. Occasionally a message cannot be processed successfully even after several retries, and the team wants to isolate those messages for later analysis without blocking the main queue. What should be configured?
options: A. Configure a dead-letter queue (DLQ) on the main SQS queue and set a maximum receive count. After the threshold is reached, messages are automatically moved to the DLQ.
B. Use Amazon SNS instead of SQS.
C. Delete messages that fail processing immediately.
D. Increase the visibility timeout to the maximum value.

question: A company hosts a static website on Amazon S3. They want the website to remain available even if the primary S3 bucket or the Region becomes unavailable. Which architecture provides the highest availability?
options: A. An S3 bucket behind an Application Load Balancer.
B. Hosting the website on a single EC2 instance.
C. A single S3 bucket with versioning enabled.
D. Two S3 buckets in different Regions, with Amazon CloudFront configured with origin failover (primary and secondary origins), and Route 53 health checks if needed.

question: An application runs on Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type. The service must be able to survive the failure of an Availability Zone. How should the service be configured?
options: A. Configure the ECS service to use multiple subnets across at least two Availability Zones and set the desired count high enough that tasks can be redistributed if one AZ fails. Use a load balancer that spans the same AZs.

C. Disable cross-zone load balancing.
D. Deploy the service in a single AZ and increase the number of tasks.

question: A company has an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. They need to scale read capacity for reporting queries without impacting the primary transactional workload, and they also need automatic failover if the primary instance fails. Which Aurora configuration should be used?

B. Two independent Aurora clusters with application-level failover logic only.
C. An Aurora DB cluster with a primary instance and at least one Aurora Replica. Use the cluster endpoint for writes and the reader endpoint for reads. Multi-AZ is inherent in the storage layer.

question: A Solutions Architect is designing a system that processes financial transactions. The system must not lose any messages even if a processing component fails, and messages must be processed in the order they were received for each customer. Which Amazon SQS configuration is required?
options: A. Standard queue with long polling.

question: An organization needs a shared file system that can be mounted concurrently by hundreds of EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones and must remain available if one AZ fails. Which service meets this requirement?

D. Move the origin to Amazon S3 only.

question: A company runs batch jobs on Amazon EC2 that can take several hours to complete. Occasionally an instance fails midway through a job. The company wants failed jobs to be retried automatically without manual intervention. Which service combination provides a resilient solution?

B. A single EC2 instance that runs a cron job.
C. Amazon ECS tasks without any retry logic.

D. AWS Batch with a managed compute environment, job queues, and job definitions that specify retry strategies. Alternatively, Step Functions with error handling and retries, or an SQS-based worker pattern with a DLQ.

question: A Solutions Architect is designing the networking for a highly available application. The application requires low-latency communication between instances. Which placement strategy should be used carefully, and what is the trade-off?
options: A. No placement group is ever needed.
B. Partition placement group guarantees the lowest possible latency.
C. Spread placement group only — always the best for both latency and availability.
D. Cluster placement group — provides the lowest latency but concentrates instances in a single AZ, reducing availability if that AZ fails.

question: An application uses Amazon SQS Standard queues. Under rare conditions the same message is delivered more than once. The application must handle this without creating duplicate records in the database. What is the recommended approach?
options: A. Disable long polling.
B. Design the application to be idempotent — for example by using a unique transaction ID as a primary key or by checking whether the work has already been performed before writing to the database.
C. Switch to a FIFO queue only and never use Standard queues.
D. Reduce the visibility timeout to 1 second.

question: A company has a requirement that their critical application must have an RPO of 5 minutes and an RTO of 30 minutes in the event of a Regional failure. Which disaster recovery strategy is appropriate and cost-effective?
options: A. Pilot light with only backups and no running infrastructure.
B. Active-active with full capacity in both Regions at all times (highest cost).
C. Backup and restore with daily backups only.

D. Warm standby: a scaled-down but fully functional environment running in a second Region, with continuous or frequent data replication (for example Aurora global database or DynamoDB global tables). Scale up and fail over using Route 53 when needed.

question: An Auto Scaling group is used with an Application Load Balancer. The company observes that when an instance fails its health check, it continues to receive traffic for a short period. How can this be improved?
options: A. Use only EC2 status checks and ignore ELB health checks.
B. Increase the desired capacity permanently.
C. Disable health checks on the target group.

question: A company wants to protect its application from the failure of a single EC2 instance and from the failure of an entire Availability Zone. The application is currently deployed on two instances in one AZ. What is the minimum change required?

D. Move both instances to a different AZ.

question: A serverless application uses Amazon EventBridge to route events to multiple Lambda functions. Occasionally one of the downstream functions fails. The team wants failed events to be captured for later analysis without losing them. What should be configured?

D. Use only synchronous invocations and ignore errors.

question: An organization runs a legacy application that must keep state on the local file system. options: A. Amazon EBS volumes (standard single-attach).

D. Amazon S3 with the AWS SDK only.

question: A cloud architect is designing a multi-Region active-passive architecture. The database is Amazon Aurora. Which Aurora feature provides the lowest RPO for cross-Region replication?
options: A. Manual snapshot copy every hour.

question: An organization runs a critical web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application currently runs in a single Availability Zone. question: An e-commerce application processes orders asynchronously. During peak sales events the order volume can increase by 20x. C. Add more web servers and keep the synchronous database writes.
D. Replace the relational database with a single Amazon DynamoDB table and keep synchronous writes from the web tier.

question: An organization uses Amazon RDS for MySQL as the primary database for a production application. The Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is 5 minutes and the Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is near zero. Which configuration BEST meets these requirements?

question: A microservices application uses Amazon SQS for inter-service communication. Occasionally a message cannot be processed successfully even after several retries, and the team wants to isolate those messages for later analysis without blocking the main queue. What should be configured?

C. Use Amazon SNS instead of SQS.
D. Increase the visibility timeout to the maximum value.

question: An application runs on Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type. The service must be able to survive the failure of an Availability Zone. How should the service be configured?

question: An Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group is used for a stateful application that stores session data on the local disk. When instances are terminated during scale-in, users lose their sessions. How can this be resolved while still using Auto Scaling?

question: An organization needs to ensure that its Amazon Aurora database can survive the failure of an entire Availability Zone with minimal downtime. What is the recommended configuration?

question: A global application uses Amazon CloudFront. The origin is an Application Load Balancer in a single Region. The company wants the application to remain available if that Region fails. Which approach provides origin failover capability?

question: A company runs batch jobs on Amazon EC2 that can take several hours to complete. Occasionally an instance fails midway through a job. The company wants failed jobs to be retried automatically without manual intervention. Which service combination provides a resilient solution?

C. A single EC2 instance that runs a cron job.

question: A Solutions Architect is designing the networking for a highly available application. The application requires low-latency communication between instances. Which placement strategy should be used carefully, and what is the trade-off?

question: An application uses Amazon SQS Standard queues. Under rare conditions the same message is delivered more than once. The application must handle this without creating duplicate records in the database. What is the recommended approach?

question: A company has a requirement that their critical application must have an RPO of 5 minutes and an RTO of 30 minutes in the event of a Regional failure. Which disaster recovery strategy is appropriate and cost-effective?

question: An Auto Scaling group is used with an Application Load Balancer. The company observes that when an instance fails its health check, it continues to receive traffic for a short period. How can this be improved?

question: A serverless application uses Amazon EventBridge to route events to multiple Lambda functions. Occasionally one of the downstream functions fails. The team wants failed events to be captured for later analysis without losing them. What should be configured?

D. Single-AZ RDS with one read replica in the same AZ.

question: A Solutions Architect must design a solution for processing images uploaded by users. The processing can take several minutes and must not be lost if a worker fails. The system should automatically scale based on the number of pending images. Which architecture is MOST resilient and scalable?
options: A. Users upload images to an EBS volume attached to a single EC2 instance.

B. Users upload images to Amazon S3. S3 event notifications send a message to an SQS queue. An Auto Scaling group of EC2 workers (or Lambda functions) polls the queue, processes the images, and writes results back to S3. Failed messages go to a dead-letter queue.
C. Use a single long-running EC2 instance that polls an S3 bucket every minute.
D. Users upload images directly to an EC2 instance that processes them synchronously.

question: A company has a multi-tier application with a web tier, application tier, and database tier. They want to ensure that a failure in the web tier does not cascade and take down the entire system. Which design principle should be applied?
options: A. Tight coupling between all tiers using synchronous calls with no timeouts.
B. Using a single shared database connection pool without isolation.
C. Loose coupling using message queues (SQS) or pub/sub (SNS/EventBridge) between tiers, health checks, circuit breakers, and independent Auto Scaling for each tier.
D. Placing all tiers on the same EC2 instance.

question: An Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group is used for a stateful application that stores session data on the local disk. When instances are terminated during scale-in, users lose their sessions. How can this be resolved while still using Auto Scaling?
options: A. Use only Spot Instances so that interruptions are expected.
B. Move session state to an external shared store such as Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon ElastiCache, or a shared EFS file system, and configure the Auto Scaling group to use ELB health checks.
C. Disable scale-in completely.
D. Increase the health check grace period to 1 hour.

question: A company needs to ensure that its Amazon Aurora database can survive the failure of an entire Availability Zone with minimal downtime. What is the recommended configuration?
options: A. A single Aurora instance in one AZ.
B. Two separate Aurora clusters in the same AZ with manual failover.
C. An Aurora cluster with the primary instance and at least one replica placed in different Availability Zones. Aurora storage is already replicated across three AZs.
D. Using Amazon RDS for MySQL with a single Multi-AZ standby only, without Aurora.

question: A media company serves video files and static assets to a global audience. Users are complaining about high latency when downloading content. The origin is an S3 bucket in us-east-1. Which solution will MOST improve performance for global users?
options: A. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as the origin, enable appropriate caching, and optionally use S3 Transfer Acceleration for uploads.
B. Copy the entire bucket to every AWS Region and use Route 53 geolocation routing.
C. Move the bucket to a single Region closer to the majority of users and accept higher latency for others.
D. Increase the S3 bucket storage class to S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

question: An application experiences a sudden 10x increase in read traffic to its Amazon RDS MySQL database during peak hours, causing CPU saturation and slow responses. The write volume remains low and steady. What is the MOST effective way to improve read performance?
options: A. Enable Multi-AZ on the primary instance.
B. Create one or more read replicas and configure the application to send read queries to the replica endpoints (or use a reader endpoint if using Aurora).
C. Change the instance class of the primary to a much larger size.
D. Switch the storage type to magnetic.

question: A high-performance computing (HPC) workload needs to run tightly coupled simulations across dozens of EC2 instances. The instances require extremely low latency and high bandwidth network communication. Which configuration is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Place each instance in a different Availability Zone and use a Network Load Balancer.
B. Use T3 burstable instances with standard networking.
C. Distribute the instances across multiple Regions for higher availability.

D. Launch the instances in a cluster placement group within a single Availability Zone, use an instance type that supports enhanced networking (ENA) and preferably Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA), and select a network-optimized instance family (for example C5n, C6i, or HPC-oriented types).

question: A web application serves personalized content and product recommendations. Response times are currently 800–1200 ms, and the business wants to reduce this to under 200 ms for the majority of users. Database queries are the main bottleneck. Which combination of services is MOST likely to achieve the target?
options: A. Keep the existing architecture and simply increase the RDS instance size.
B. Replace the database with Amazon S3.

C. Introduce Amazon ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) to cache frequent queries and session data, add CloudFront for static assets, and consider DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) if the data layer moves to DynamoDB.
D. Move the entire application to a single large EC2 instance.

question: An analytics team needs to ingest and process millions of events per second from IoT devices and click streams with low latency. The data must be available for real-time dashboards and also stored for later batch processing. Which AWS service is the BEST fit for the ingestion layer?
options: A. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams (or Amazon MSK if Kafka compatibility is required).
B. Amazon SQS Standard queues.
C. Amazon S3 with multipart uploads only.
D. Amazon SNS with email subscriptions.

question: A company has an Application Load Balancer distributing traffic to EC2 instances. They want to route requests for /api/* to one target group and requests for /static/* to another target group that serves content from a different set of instances (or from S3 via a different architecture). Which ALB feature enables this?
options: A. Path-based routing (and optionally host-based routing) rules on the listener.
B. Network Load Balancer cross-zone load balancing.
C. Classic Load Balancer only.
D. Sticky sessions only.

question: A database workload on Amazon EC2 requires consistent high IOPS (tens of thousands) and low latency for random read/write operations. Which Amazon EBS volume type should be selected?
options: A. Cold HDD (sc1).
B. Throughput Optimized HDD (st1).
C. Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1 or io2 / io2 Block Express) sized for the required IOPS and throughput.
D. General Purpose SSD (gp2) without any provisioned capacity.

question: A mobile gaming company needs to store and retrieve player session data with microsecond latency. The data is simple key-value pairs and is accessed extremely frequently. Which service is the BEST fit?
options: A. Amazon S3 with Transfer Acceleration.
B. Amazon RDS for MySQL with a large instance class.
C. Amazon Glacier Instant Retrieval.
D. Amazon ElastiCache for Redis (or MemoryDB for Redis if durability is also required).

question: Users in Asia and Europe are uploading large media files to an S3 bucket in us-east-1 and experiencing slow upload speeds. Which S3 feature can improve upload performance without requiring the users to change their upload tool significantly?
options: A. Disabling multipart uploads.
B. S3 Transfer Acceleration, which routes uploads through CloudFront edge locations.
C. S3 One Zone-IA.
D. S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class.

question: An application uses Amazon DynamoDB and is experiencing hot partitions and throttling under heavy write load. The partition key is a low-cardinality attribute (for example status = "active"). What is the MOST effective remediation?
options: A. Switch to eventually consistent reads.
B. Increase the provisioned write capacity units only.

C. Redesign the partition key to have higher cardinality (for example include a random suffix, a timestamp component, or a more unique identifier) so that writes are distributed evenly across partitions. Consider write sharding if necessary.
D. Enable DynamoDB Streams.

question: A company wants to serve both static assets and a dynamic API from the same domain name with low latency worldwide. Which architecture is recommended?
options: A. Amazon S3 static website hosting only.
B. A single EC2 instance in one Region with a public IP.
C. Route 53 latency routing to different ALBs without a CDN.

D. Amazon CloudFront with multiple origins (S3 for static content, API Gateway or ALB for the dynamic API), using cache behaviors to route paths appropriately, and Lambda@Edge or CloudFront Functions if light request manipulation is needed at the edge.

question: A data processing pipeline needs to read a large CSV file stored in S3 and extract only a subset of rows and columns for further processing. Transferring the entire object every time is expensive and slow. Which feature can improve performance and reduce cost?
options: A. Downloading the full object and filtering client-side every time.
B. S3 Select (or S3 Glacier Select for archived objects) to retrieve only the required data using SQL-like expressions.
C. Moving the object to Glacier Deep Archive permanently.
D. Enabling S3 Versioning.

question: An application requires a shared, high-throughput file system that can be accessed concurrently by thousands of EC2 instances for a machine-learning training job. Which storage service is designed for this use case?
options: A. Amazon S3 with the AWS SDK only.
B. Amazon FSx for Lustre, which is optimized for high-performance computing and can be linked to S3 for long-term storage.
C. Amazon EBS gp3 volumes attached to each instance independently.
D. Amazon EFS with the default bursting mode and no performance considerations.

question: An organization observes that their Amazon CloudFront distribution has a low cache hit ratio for dynamic content. What actions can improve the cache hit ratio?
options: A. Use only signed URLs without any caching configuration.
B. Disable caching entirely so that every request goes to the origin.
C. Review and optimize cache keys (query strings, headers, cookies), set appropriate TTLs via Cache-Control headers or CloudFront cache policies, and consider Origin Shield for multi-Region origins.
D. Increase the origin request timeout to the maximum.

question: A real-time bidding application needs to handle hundreds of thousands of requests per second with consistent single-digit millisecond latency. Which load balancer and compute combination is MOST suitable?
options: A. Application Load Balancer with T3 instances.

C. Amazon API Gateway with Lambda only, without any performance testing.
D. Classic Load Balancer with a single large instance.
