B. Increase the size of the primary instance only.
C. Switch to a single-AZ deployment to reduce latency.
D. Disable Multi-AZ.

D. AWS Lambda with 15-minute timeouts for multi-hour Spark jobs.

B. Increase the minimum capacity of the Auto Scaling group permanently to the peak level.

question: An application needs to query large amounts of structured data stored in S3 without managing any infrastructure. Query latency of a few seconds is acceptable. Which service is designed for this?
options: A. Amazon EC2 with a self-managed database.
B. Amazon RDS with the data loaded into a single large instance.
C. Amazon Redshift Spectrum or Amazon Athena (serverless SQL queries directly on S3 data).
D. Amazon DynamoDB with a scan operation on every query.

question: An organization is running a containerized microservices application on Amazon EKS. Some services need to communicate with extremely low latency. Which networking approach is recommended for high performance?
options: A. Use the Amazon VPC CNI plugin (or an alternative high-performance CNI), consider AWS App Mesh or Kubernetes native service discovery, and place latency-sensitive pods in the same Availability Zone when possible. For the highest performance, evaluate VPC Lattice or host-mode networking carefully.

C. Use only ClusterIP services with no consideration of AZ placement.

question: A data lake on S3 is queried frequently by multiple teams using different tools. Some queries scan the same large datasets repeatedly. What can improve performance and reduce cost?

question: An application uses Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. Under load, some clients experience high latency. The team has already optimized the Lambda code. What additional steps can improve performance?

C. Disable all caching and force every request to hit Lambda.
D. Replace API Gateway with a single EC2 instance.

question: An application is experiencing high latency when reading frequently accessed data from Amazon DynamoDB. The table is already provisioned with sufficient capacity. What can further reduce latency?

D. Enabling S3 Versioning.

question: An application requires a shared, high-throughput file system that can be accessed concurrently by thousands of EC2 instances for a machine-learning training job. Which storage service is designed for this use case?

D. Amazon EFS with the default bursting mode and no performance considerations.

question: A real-time bidding application needs to handle hundreds of thousands of requests per second with consistent single-digit millisecond latency. Which load balancer and compute combination is MOST suitable?

question: A company has a large amount of data in S3 Standard that is accessed infrequently and can tolerate a retrieval time of a few hours. Which storage class change will reduce cost the most while still meeting the access requirements?

question: An organization has multiple AWS accounts. Each account receives its own invoice, and the company is missing out on volume discounts. What should they implement to reduce overall cost?

question: A batch processing workload runs for several hours each night and can tolerate interruption. The company wants the lowest possible compute cost. Which EC2 purchasing option should be the primary choice?
options: A. Spot Instances (or Spot Fleet / Auto Scaling with Spot), with a fallback to On-Demand if capacity is unavailable, and a design that can resume or restart interrupted jobs.

D. Standard Reserved Instances for 3 years.

question: An application generates a large number of small log files that are written to S3 every few seconds. The company has noticed high request costs (PUT requests). How can the cost of writing the logs be reduced?

D. Continue writing every small file individually.

question: A company has a large number of Amazon EBS snapshots that are no longer needed. They also have unattached EBS volumes. What actions will reduce storage costs?

C. Leave all snapshots and volumes in place indefinitely.
D. Create more frequent snapshots of every volume.

question: A serverless application uses AWS Lambda and Amazon API Gateway. The functions are invoked infrequently but the team has configured provisioned concurrency for all of them at a high level. The bill is higher than expected. What should be reviewed?

question: A company is using NAT Gateways in every Availability Zone for a large number of private subnets. The data transfer and hourly charges for the NAT Gateways are significant. What are valid cost-optimization strategies?

question: An organization wants to track cost by project, environment (dev/test/prod), and business unit. They currently have no consistent tagging strategy. What is the recommended first step?

question: A company has a containerized application running on Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type. The tasks are over-provisioned with CPU and memory. What should the Solutions Architect recommend?

D. Switch to the largest possible Fargate configuration for every task.

question: A data warehouse on Amazon Redshift is used heavily during business hours but is almost idle at night and on weekends. How can the company reduce cost while keeping the cluster available when needed?
options: A. Delete the cluster every evening and restore from snapshot every morning.
B. Switch to Amazon Athena for all workloads without evaluating query patterns.

question: An organization is transferring large amounts of data from on-premises data centers to Amazon S3. C. Disable the cache entirely.

options: A. S3 Express One Zone (high-performance, higher cost).
B. S3 Standard.
C. S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) or S3 One Zone-IA (if the data is recreatable and single-AZ is acceptable).
D. S3 Glacier Deep Archive (retrieval in hours).

question: An organization runs a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances that process steady, predictable workloads 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The instances are currently all On-Demand. The finance team has asked for a significant reduction in compute cost without changing the application or the instance types. What should the Solutions Architect recommend?
options: A. Switch all instances to Spot Instances immediately.

B. Purchase Compute Savings Plans or Standard/Convertible Reserved Instances that match the instance family, Region, and term (1 or 3 years) that best fit the commitment the company is willing to make.
C. Terminate half of the instances and hope the remaining ones can handle the load.
D. Move the workloads to AWS Lambda without any analysis of suitability.

question: A data analytics company stores large volumes of log data in Amazon S3. The data is frequently accessed for the first 30 days, occasionally accessed for the next 60 days, and almost never accessed after 90 days, but must be retained for 7 years for compliance. How should the storage be optimized for cost?
options: A. Keep all objects in S3 Standard for the entire 7 years.

B. Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration that transitions objects to S3 Standard-IA (or Intelligent-Tiering) after 30 days, to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval or Deep Archive after 90 days, and expires or transitions to a compliant archive after the retention period if appropriate.
C. Move everything to S3 Glacier Deep Archive immediately after upload.
D. Store the data on EBS volumes attached to a single EC2 instance.

question: A development team has a set of Amazon EC2 instances and RDS databases that are only needed during business hours (Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–6 p.m.). Outside these hours the resources sit idle but continue to incur charges. What is the MOST cost-effective approach?
options: A. Leave all resources running 24/7 on On-Demand pricing.
B. Terminate the instances every evening and recreate them from AMIs every morning manually.

C. Use AWS Instance Scheduler (or a custom Lambda + CloudWatch Events solution) to automatically stop EC2 instances and stop/start RDS instances outside business hours. Consider Aurora Serverless or smaller instance sizes for development.
D. Purchase 3-year Reserved Instances for the development environment.

question: A company has many Amazon EC2 instances of various sizes and families. Some are over-provisioned and rarely use more than 20% of their CPU or memory. Which AWS service provides specific rightsizing recommendations?
options: A. AWS Budgets alone.
B. AWS Compute Optimizer (and Trusted Advisor checks for underutilized resources).
C. Amazon CloudWatch only, without any analysis engine.
D. AWS Cost Explorer with no additional features.

question: A company is designing a new application that will have highly variable and unpredictable traffic. Sometimes the load is near zero for hours; at other times it spikes dramatically. Which compute approach is likely to be the MOST cost-effective?
options: A. A fixed fleet of large Reserved Instances sized for peak load.

B. A combination of AWS Lambda (for event-driven or API workloads) and/or EC2 Auto Scaling with a mix of On-Demand and Spot capacity, or Aurora Serverless / Fargate for appropriate components, so that the company pays mainly for what is actually consumed.
C. A single very large EC2 instance running continuously.
D. Dedicated Hosts for the entire application.

question: An organization has a large amount of data in S3 Standard that is accessed infrequently and can tolerate a retrieval time of a few hours. Which storage class change will reduce cost the most while still meeting the access requirements?
options: A. Transition the data to S3 Standard-IA or S3 One Zone-IA if the data is non-critical and can live in a single AZ.
B. Move the data to Amazon EBS Cold HDD volumes.
C. Transition the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
D. Keep the data in S3 Standard and enable versioning.

question: An organization has multiple AWS accounts. Each account receives its own invoice, and the company is missing out on volume discounts. What should they implement to reduce overall cost?
options: A. Merge all workloads into a single AWS account regardless of security or operational boundaries.
B. Keep the accounts completely separate and negotiate individual discounts.
C. Create an AWS Organization and enable consolidated billing so that usage is aggregated for pricing tiers and Reserved Instance / Savings Plans discounts can be shared (where applicable).
D. Use only the AWS Free Tier for all accounts.

question: A batch processing workload runs for several hours each night and can tolerate interruption. The company wants the lowest possible compute cost. Which EC2 purchasing option should be the primary choice?
options: A. Standard Reserved Instances for 3 years.
B. Spot Instances (or Spot Fleet / Auto Scaling with Spot), with a fallback to On-Demand if capacity is unavailable, and a design that can resume or restart interrupted jobs.
C. Dedicated Hosts.
D. On-Demand Instances.

question: A company is paying a significant amount for data transfer out to the internet from their application. The application serves static and dynamic content to users worldwide. What architectural change is MOST likely to reduce data transfer costs?
options: A. Use only public IPv4 addresses and avoid IPv6.
B. Disable all compression on the application.

C. Place Amazon CloudFront in front of the application and S3 origins so that the majority of content is served from edge locations; users closer to the edge reduce origin data transfer, and CloudFront data transfer pricing is often more favorable.
D. Move all EC2 instances to a single Availability Zone.

question: A development team frequently launches large EC2 instances for short-lived tests and forgets to terminate them. This has resulted in unexpected bills. Which combination of tools can help prevent this?
options: A. Only manual review of the billing console once a month.
B. Disabling the EC2 service in development accounts.
C. Purchasing Reserved Instances for every possible instance type.

D. AWS Budgets with alerts, AWS Instance Scheduler or automated Lambda functions to stop/terminate idle instances, tagging policies, and optionally Service Control Policies that restrict the instance types that can be launched in non-production accounts.

question: A company uses Amazon RDS for a production database that runs 24/7 with a stable load. They are currently using On-Demand pricing. What is the simplest way to reduce the database cost significantly?
options: A. Move the database to a single EC2 instance running MySQL.
B. Switch to a much smaller instance class without testing.
C. Disable Multi-AZ and automated backups.
D. Purchase an RDS Reserved Instance (or use Savings Plans where applicable) for the instance class and Region in use.

question: An application generates a large number of small log files that are written to S3 every few seconds. The company has noticed high request costs (PUT requests). How can the cost of writing the logs be reduced?
options: A. Disable logging entirely.
B. Continue writing every small file individually.
C. Write the logs to an EBS volume instead of S3.

D. Buffer the log records and write larger objects less frequently (for example using Kinesis Data Firehose with S3 as the destination, or an application-side buffer), and consider using S3 Intelligent-Tiering or lifecycle policies for the resulting objects.

question: An organization has a large number of Amazon EBS snapshots that are no longer needed. They also have unattached EBS volumes. What actions will reduce storage costs?
options: A. Move all snapshots to S3 Glacier manually without a lifecycle policy.
B. Create more frequent snapshots of every volume.
C. Leave all snapshots and volumes in place indefinitely.

D. Delete unnecessary snapshots and unattached volumes. Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (DLM) or AWS Backup policies to automate retention going forward. Consider converting gp2 volumes to gp3 for better price/performance.

question: A serverless application uses AWS Lambda and Amazon API Gateway. The functions are invoked infrequently but the team has configured provisioned concurrency for all of them at a high level. The bill is higher than expected. What should be reviewed?
options: A. Replace Lambda with always-on EC2 instances.
B. Switch every function to the maximum memory setting.

C. Right-size or remove unnecessary provisioned concurrency; use it only for functions that truly require consistent low latency and have predictable traffic. For spiky or low-traffic functions, on-demand concurrency is usually more cost-effective.
D. Increase provisioned concurrency further to improve performance.

question: A company is using NAT Gateways in every Availability Zone for a large number of private subnets. The data transfer and hourly charges for the NAT Gateways are significant. What are valid cost-optimization strategies?
options: A. Replace all NAT Gateways with internet gateways on private subnets.
B. Keep a NAT Gateway in every AZ regardless of actual traffic patterns.
C. Disable all private subnet route tables.

D. Evaluate whether VPC endpoints (gateway endpoints for S3/DynamoDB, interface endpoints for other services) can eliminate the need for NAT for a large portion of the traffic; consider a shared NAT Gateway design where appropriate; review whether all subnets truly need outbound internet access.

question: An organization wants to track cost by project, environment (dev/test/prod), and business unit. They currently have no consistent tagging strategy. What is the recommended first step?
options: A. Create a separate AWS account for every project without any tagging.

B. Define a mandatory tagging policy (for example Project, Environment, Owner, CostCenter), enforce it with AWS Organizations Service Control Policies or IAM policies, activate cost allocation tags in Billing, and use Cost Explorer and Cost and Usage Reports to analyze spend by tag.
C. Use only the AWS Free Tier and avoid any cost analysis.
D. Ignore tagging and only look at the total bill.

question: A company has a containerized application running on Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type. The tasks are over-provisioned with CPU and memory. What should the Solutions Architect recommend?
options: A. Move everything back to EC2 without any analysis.
B. Switch to the largest possible Fargate configuration for every task.
C. Leave the task definitions at their current large sizes.
D. Analyze CloudWatch Container Insights or Container Metrics, right-size the task CPU and memory values, and consider Savings Plans for Fargate or Fargate Spot for interruptible workloads.

question: A data warehouse on Amazon Redshift is used heavily during business hours but is almost idle at night and on weekends. How can the company reduce cost while keeping the cluster available when needed?
options: A. Leave the cluster running at full size 24/7.
B. Delete the cluster every evening and restore from snapshot every morning.
C. Switch to Amazon Athena for all workloads without evaluating query patterns.
D. Use Redshift’s pause and resume capability (or Elastic Resize / Classic Resize to a smaller size during off-hours), or consider Redshift Serverless if the usage pattern fits.

question: An organization is transferring large amounts of data from on-premises data centers to Amazon S3. They are currently using the public internet and paying significant egress charges to their ISP as well as experiencing slow transfer rates. Which AWS service can reduce both cost and transfer time for multi-terabyte or petabyte-scale migrations?
options: A. Use AWS DataSync or AWS Snow Family devices (Snowball, Snowball Edge, Snowmobile) depending on the data volume and network bandwidth, or establish an AWS Direct Connect connection for ongoing large transfers.
B. Continue using the public internet with multiple parallel streams only.
C. Use only single-threaded SCP over the internet.
D. Email the data on hard drives without any tracking.

question: An application uses Amazon ElastiCache for Redis. The cache is running on a large node type 24/7, but CloudWatch metrics show that memory utilization is consistently below 30% and CPU is low. What should be done?
options: A. Switch to a multi-AZ configuration with three times the capacity without analysis.
B. Disable the cache entirely.
C. Increase the node type to the next larger size.
D. Right-size the node type based on the observed utilization, and consider Reserved Nodes if the cache will run continuously for a year or more.

question: A company has enabled detailed monitoring (1-minute metrics) for all EC2 instances and has hundreds of custom CloudWatch metrics. The CloudWatch bill is higher than expected. How can costs be reduced without losing essential visibility?
options: A. Keep detailed monitoring and all custom metrics indefinitely.
B. Send every log line as a separate custom metric.

C. Switch non-critical instances to basic monitoring (5-minute metrics), reduce the number of custom metrics, use metric filters and aggregation where possible, and set appropriate retention periods for logs. Evaluate whether Contributor Insights or other advanced features are necessary.
D. Disable all CloudWatch monitoring.

question: An organization is using Amazon S3 for a data lake. They have many small objects (a few KB each), which increases the cost of LIST and GET requests and also affects performance. What optimization can help?
options: A. Aggregate small objects into larger objects (for example using file formats such as Parquet with row groups, or simply concatenating files), and use S3 Inventory or S3 Batch Operations for management. Consider S3 Intelligent-Tiering for automatic cost optimization of the resulting objects.

C. Move every small object to Glacier Instant Retrieval.
D. Keep every record as an individual object.

question: An organization has a three-year commitment window and a very stable EC2 footprint. They want the maximum discount available. Which purchasing option typically provides the highest savings?
options: A. Dedicated Hosts without any reservation.
B. Spot Instances for non-interruptible production workloads.
C. On-Demand Instances.
D. 3-year All Upfront Standard Reserved Instances or the equivalent Compute Savings Plans with a 3-year all-upfront commitment.

question: An application currently runs on a fleet of m5.2xlarge On-Demand instances. After analyzing utilization, the team determines that m5.xlarge instances would be sufficient. question: An organization is using AWS Lambda for a high-volume API. They notice that a large percentage of the cost is from a few functions that process large payloads and run for several seconds. How can they reduce cost?

question: A company has a multi-account environment and wants to ensure that developers cannot launch expensive GPU instances in non-production accounts. How can this be enforced centrally?

question: An analytics workload uses Amazon Athena to query data in S3. The queries are scanning far more data than necessary, resulting in high costs. What practices will reduce Athena query costs?

question: A company is running a production application on EC2 and wants to reduce cost while maintaining the ability to handle unexpected load spikes. Which strategy balances cost and performance?

question: A company has enabled AWS Cost Explorer and is reviewing the “RI/SP Coverage” and “RI/SP Utilization” reports. They notice that a significant portion of their compute usage is still On-Demand even though they have purchased Savings Plans. What should they investigate?

question: An organization has a multi-account environment and wants to ensure that developers cannot launch expensive GPU instances in non-production accounts. How can this be enforced centrally?
options: A. Use AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) to deny the launch of specific instance types (or families) in the non-production organizational units or accounts.

D. Remove the EC2 service from all non-production accounts.

question: An analytics workload uses Amazon Athena to query data in S3. The queries are scanning far more data than necessary, resulting in high costs. What practices will reduce Athena query costs?

question: A company is running a production application on EC2 and wants to reduce cost while maintaining the ability to handle unexpected load spikes. Which strategy balances cost and performance?
options: A. Run a fixed number of the largest possible On-Demand instances at all times.
B. Disable Auto Scaling and manually launch instances when needed.
C. Run only Spot Instances with no On-Demand capacity.

D. Use an Auto Scaling group with a base of Reserved / Savings Plans capacity (or On-Demand) sized for the typical load, and allow the group to scale out using Spot Instances (with diversification across instance types and AZs) for the variable portion of demand. Use a suitable scaling policy.

question: A company has enabled AWS Cost Explorer and is reviewing the “RI/SP Coverage” and “RI/SP Utilization” reports. They notice that a significant portion of their compute usage is still On-Demand even though they have purchased Savings Plans. What should they investigate?
options: A. Whether the Savings Plans type (Compute vs EC2 Instance), term, payment option, and the actual usage patterns (Region, instance family, etc.) are aligned. They may need additional Savings Plans or to adjust the mix of instance types to better match the existing commitment.
B. Switch everything to Spot Instances only.
C. Nothing — Savings Plans automatically cover every possible usage.
D. Cancel all Savings Plans immediately.

question: A company stores infrequently accessed documents in S3 and wants to minimize storage cost while keeping the documents available for retrieval within minutes if needed. Which storage class is the MOST cost-effective choice?
options: A. S3 Glacier Deep Archive (retrieval in hours).
B. S3 Express One Zone (high-performance, higher cost).
C. S3 Standard.
D. S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) or S3 One Zone-IA (if the data is recreatable and single-AZ is acceptable).

question: A company runs a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances that process steady, predictable workloads 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The instances are currently all On-Demand. options: A. Switch all instances to Spot Instances immediately.

B. Purchase Compute Savings Plans or Standard/Convertible Reserved Instances that match the instance family, Region, and term (1 or 3 years) that best fit the commitment the company is willing to make.
C. Move the workloads to AWS Lambda without any analysis of suitability.
D. Terminate half of the instances and hope the remaining ones can handle the load.

question: A data analytics company stores large volumes of log data in Amazon S3. B. Move everything to S3 Glacier Deep Archive immediately after upload.

C. Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration that transitions objects to S3 Standard-IA (or Intelligent-Tiering) after 30 days, to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval or Deep Archive after 90 days, and expires or transitions to a compliant archive after the retention period if appropriate.
D. Store the data on EBS volumes attached to a single EC2 instance.

question: A development team has a set of Amazon EC2 instances and RDS databases that are only needed during business hours (Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–6 p.m.). Outside these hours the resources sit idle but continue to incur charges. What is the MOST cost-effective approach?
options: A. Leave all resources running 24/7 on On-Demand pricing.
B. Purchase 3-year Reserved Instances for the development environment.

D. Terminate the instances every evening and recreate them from AMIs every morning manually.

options: A. AWS Cost Explorer with no additional features.

D. AWS Budgets alone.

question: An organization is designing a new application that will have highly variable and unpredictable traffic. Sometimes the load is near zero for hours; at other times it spikes dramatically. Which compute approach is likely to be the MOST cost-effective?
options: A. A combination of AWS Lambda (for event-driven or API workloads) and/or EC2 Auto Scaling with a mix of On-Demand and Spot capacity, or Aurora Serverless / Fargate for appropriate components, so that the company pays mainly for what is actually consumed.
B. Dedicated Hosts for the entire application.
C. A single very large EC2 instance running continuously.
D. A fixed fleet of large Reserved Instances sized for peak load.

question: A company has a large amount of data in S3 Standard that is accessed infrequently and can tolerate a retrieval time of a few hours. Which storage class change will reduce cost the most while still meeting the access requirements?
options: A. Transition the data to S3 Standard-IA or S3 One Zone-IA if the data is non-critical and can live in a single AZ.
B. Move the data to Amazon EBS Cold HDD volumes.
C. Keep the data in S3 Standard and enable versioning.
D. Transition the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

question: An organization has multiple AWS accounts. Each account receives its own invoice, and the company is missing out on volume discounts. What should they implement to reduce overall cost?
options: A. Merge all workloads into a single AWS account regardless of security or operational boundaries.

C. Create an AWS Organization and enable consolidated billing so that usage is aggregated for pricing tiers and Reserved Instance / Savings Plans discounts can be shared (where applicable).
D. Keep the accounts completely separate and negotiate individual discounts.

question: A batch processing workload runs for several hours each night and can tolerate interruption. The company wants the lowest possible compute cost. Which EC2 purchasing option should be the primary choice?
options: A. On-Demand Instances.

C. Dedicated Hosts.
D. Standard Reserved Instances for 3 years.

question: An organization is paying a significant amount for data transfer out to the internet from their application. The application serves static and dynamic content to users worldwide. What architectural change is MOST likely to reduce data transfer costs?

B. Use only public IPv4 addresses and avoid IPv6.

D. Move all EC2 instances to a single Availability Zone.

question: A development team frequently launches large EC2 instances for short-lived tests and forgets to terminate them. This has resulted in unexpected bills. Which combination of tools can help prevent this?
options: A. Purchasing Reserved Instances for every possible instance type.

D. Disabling the EC2 service in development accounts.

question: An organization uses Amazon RDS for a production database that runs 24/7 with a stable load. They are currently using On-Demand pricing. What is the simplest way to reduce the database cost significantly?

D. Disable Multi-AZ and automated backups.

question: An application generates a large number of small log files that are written to S3 every few seconds. The company has noticed high request costs (PUT requests). How can the cost of writing the logs be reduced?

question: A company has a large number of Amazon EBS snapshots that are no longer needed. They also have unattached EBS volumes. What actions will reduce storage costs?

question: An organization is using NAT Gateways in every Availability Zone for a large number of private subnets. The data transfer and hourly charges for the NAT Gateways are significant. What are valid cost-optimization strategies?

question: A company has a containerized application running on Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type. The tasks are over-provisioned with CPU and memory. What should the Solutions Architect recommend?

question: A data warehouse on Amazon Redshift is used heavily during business hours but is almost idle at night and on weekends. How can the company reduce cost while keeping the cluster available when needed?

C. Switch non-critical instances to basic monitoring (5-minute metrics), reduce the number of custom metrics, use metric filters and aggregation where possible, and set appropriate retention periods for logs. Evaluate whether Contributor Insights or other advanced features are necessary.
D. Send every log line as a separate custom metric.

question: A company is using Amazon S3 for a data lake. They have many small objects (a few KB each), which increases the cost of LIST and GET requests and also affects performance. What optimization can help?
options: A. Enable versioning on every object without any lifecycle policy.
B. Move every small object to Glacier Instant Retrieval.

C. Aggregate small objects into larger objects (for example using file formats such as Parquet with row groups, or simply concatenating files), and use S3 Inventory or S3 Batch Operations for management. Consider S3 Intelligent-Tiering for automatic cost optimization of the resulting objects.
D. Keep every record as an individual object.

question: A company has a three-year commitment window and a very stable EC2 footprint. They want the maximum discount available. Which purchasing option typically provides the highest savings?
options: A. 3-year All Upfront Standard Reserved Instances or the equivalent Compute Savings Plans with a 3-year all-upfront commitment.
B. On-Demand Instances.
C. Spot Instances for non-interruptible production workloads.
D. Dedicated Hosts without any reservation.

question: An application currently runs on a fleet of m5.2xlarge On-Demand instances. After analyzing utilization, the team determines that m5.xlarge instances would be sufficient. They also want to reduce cost further for the steady-state portion of the fleet. What combination of actions is recommended?
options: A. Switch everything to Spot Instances without any On-Demand or reserved capacity.
B. Keep the m5.2xlarge instances and purchase Reserved Instances for them.
C. Right-size to m5.xlarge (or the appropriate size recommended by Compute Optimizer), then purchase Savings Plans or Reserved Instances for the right-sized instances.
D. Move the application to the largest available instance type.

question: A company is using AWS Lambda for a high-volume API. They notice that a large percentage of the cost is from a few functions that process large payloads and run for several seconds. How can they reduce cost?
options: A. Profile the functions, optimize the code and dependencies, right-size the memory setting (because CPU scales with memory), and consider whether some of the work can be moved to asynchronous processing with SQS/SNS or to a container-based service if the workload is more efficient there.
B. Disable the functions during peak hours.
C. Increase the memory allocation of those functions further (which may or may not help, depending on whether the functions are CPU-bound or memory-bound).
D. Set all functions to the maximum memory of 10 GB.

question: A company has a multi-account environment and wants to ensure that developers cannot launch expensive GPU instances in non-production accounts. How can this be enforced centrally?
options: A. Use AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) to deny the launch of specific instance types (or families) in the non-production organizational units or accounts.
B. Use only CloudWatch Alarms after the instances have been launched.
C. Remove the EC2 service from all non-production accounts.
D. Ask developers politely not to launch GPU instances.

question: An analytics workload uses Amazon Athena to query data in S3. The queries are scanning far more data than necessary, resulting in high costs. What practices will reduce Athena query costs?
options: A. Convert data to columnar formats (Parquet/ORC), partition the tables by commonly filtered columns, use compression, and avoid SELECT * — only project the columns needed. Consider partitioning and file size optimization (aim for 100 MB–1 GB files).
B. Store data as large uncompressed CSV files and SELECT * on every query.
C. Move all data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive and query it directly with Athena.
D. Increase the number of Athena workers manually for every query.

question: A company is running a production application on EC2 and wants to reduce cost while maintaining the ability to handle unexpected load spikes. Which strategy balances cost and performance?
options: A. Use an Auto Scaling group with a base of Reserved / Savings Plans capacity (or On-Demand) sized for the typical load, and allow the group to scale out using Spot Instances (with diversification across instance types and AZs) for the variable portion of demand. Use a suitable scaling policy.
B. Run only Spot Instances with no On-Demand capacity.
C. Disable Auto Scaling and manually launch instances when needed.
D. Run a fixed number of the largest possible On-Demand instances at all times.

question: A company has enabled AWS Cost Explorer and is reviewing the “RI/SP Coverage” and “RI/SP Utilization” reports. They notice that a significant portion of their compute usage is still On-Demand even though they have purchased Savings Plans. What should they investigate?
options: A. Cancel all Savings Plans immediately.
B. Switch everything to Spot Instances only.
C. Nothing — Savings Plans automatically cover every possible usage.

D. Whether the Savings Plans type (Compute vs EC2 Instance), term, payment option, and the actual usage patterns (Region, instance family, etc.) are aligned. They may need additional Savings Plans or to adjust the mix of instance types to better match the existing commitment.

question: A company stores infrequently accessed documents in S3 and wants to minimize storage cost while keeping the documents available for retrieval within minutes if needed. Which storage class is the MOST cost-effective choice?
options: A. S3 Glacier Deep Archive (retrieval in hours).
B. S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) or S3 One Zone-IA (if the data is recreatable and single-AZ is acceptable).
C. S3 Express One Zone (high-performance, higher cost).
D. S3 Standard.

question: A company runs a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances that process steady, predictable workloads 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The instances are currently all On-Demand. The finance team has asked for a significant reduction in compute cost without changing the application or the instance types. What should the Solutions Architect recommend?
options: A. Move the workloads to AWS Lambda without any analysis of suitability.
B. Switch all instances to Spot Instances immediately.
C. Terminate half of the instances and hope the remaining ones can handle the load.

D. Purchase Compute Savings Plans or Standard/Convertible Reserved Instances that match the instance family, Region, and term (1 or 3 years) that best fit the commitment the company is willing to make.

question: A data analytics company stores large volumes of log data in Amazon S3. The data is frequently accessed for the first 30 days, occasionally accessed for the next 60 days, and almost never accessed after 90 days, but must be retained for 7 years for compliance. How should the storage be optimized for cost?
options: A. Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration that transitions objects to S3 Standard-IA (or Intelligent-Tiering) after 30 days, to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval or Deep Archive after 90 days, and expires or transitions to a compliant archive after the retention period if appropriate.
B. Keep all objects in S3 Standard for the entire 7 years.
C. Move everything to S3 Glacier Deep Archive immediately after upload.
D. Store the data on EBS volumes attached to a single EC2 instance.

question: A development team has a set of Amazon EC2 instances and RDS databases that are only needed during business hours (Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–6 p.m.). Outside these hours the resources sit idle but continue to incur charges. What is the most cost-effective approach?
options: A. Leave all resources running 24/7 on On-Demand pricing.
B. Purchase 3-year Reserved Instances for the development environment.
C. Terminate the instances every evening and recreate them from AMIs every morning manually.

D. Use AWS Instance Scheduler (or a custom Lambda + CloudWatch Events solution) to automatically stop EC2 instances and stop/start RDS instances outside business hours. Consider Aurora Serverless or smaller instance sizes for development.

question: A company has many Amazon EC2 instances of various sizes and families. Some are over-provisioned and rarely use more than 20% of their CPU or memory. Which AWS service provides specific rightsizing recommendations?
options: A. AWS Cost Explorer with no additional features.
B. AWS Compute Optimizer (and Trusted Advisor checks for underutilized resources).
C. AWS Budgets alone.
D. Amazon CloudWatch only, without any analysis engine.

question: A company is designing a new application that will have highly variable and unpredictable traffic. Sometimes the load is near zero for hours; at other times it spikes dramatically. Which compute approach is likely to be the most cost-effective?
options: A. A single very large EC2 instance running continuously.

B. A combination of AWS Lambda (for event-driven or API workloads) and/or EC2 Auto Scaling with a mix of On-Demand and Spot capacity, or Aurora Serverless / Fargate for appropriate components, so that the company pays mainly for what is actually consumed.
C. A fixed fleet of large Reserved Instances sized for peak load.
D. Dedicated Hosts for the entire application.

question: A company has a large amount of data in S3 Standard that is accessed infrequently and can tolerate a retrieval time of a few hours. Which storage class change will reduce cost the most while still meeting the access requirements?
options: A. Transition the data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
B. Keep the data in S3 Standard and enable versioning.
C. Move the data to Amazon EBS Cold HDD volumes.
D. Transition the data to S3 Standard-IA or S3 One Zone-IA if the data is non-critical and can live in a single AZ.

question: An organization has multiple AWS accounts. Each account receives its own invoice, and the company is missing out on volume discounts. What should they implement to reduce overall cost?
options: A. Keep the accounts completely separate and negotiate individual discounts.
B. Merge all workloads into a single AWS account regardless of security or operational boundaries.
C. Use only the AWS Free Tier for all accounts.
D. Create an AWS Organization and enable consolidated billing so that usage is aggregated for pricing tiers and Reserved Instance / Savings Plans discounts can be shared (where applicable).

question: A batch processing workload runs for several hours each night and can tolerate interruption. The company wants the lowest possible compute cost. Which EC2 purchasing option should be the primary choice?
options: A. Standard Reserved Instances for 3 years.
B. Spot Instances (or Spot Fleet / Auto Scaling with Spot), with a fallback to On-Demand if capacity is unavailable, and a design that can resume or restart interrupted jobs.
C. On-Demand Instances.
D. Dedicated Hosts.

question: A company is paying a significant amount for data transfer out to the internet from their application. The application serves static and dynamic content to users worldwide. What architectural change is MOST likely to reduce data transfer costs?
options: A. Disable all compression on the application.
B. Move all EC2 instances to a single Availability Zone.
C. Use only public IPv4 addresses and avoid IPv6.

D. Place Amazon CloudFront in front of the application and S3 origins so that the majority of content is served from edge locations; users closer to the edge reduce origin data transfer, and CloudFront data transfer pricing is often more favorable.

question: A development team frequently launches large EC2 instances for short-lived tests and forgets to terminate them. This has resulted in unexpected bills. Which combination of tools can help prevent this?
options: A. AWS Budgets with alerts, AWS Instance Scheduler or automated Lambda functions to stop/terminate idle instances, tagging policies, and optionally Service Control Policies that restrict the instance types that can be launched in non-production accounts.
B. Disabling the EC2 service in development accounts.
C. Purchasing Reserved Instances for every possible instance type.
D. Only manual review of the billing console once a month.

question: A company uses Amazon RDS for a production database that runs 24/7 with a stable load. They are currently using On-Demand pricing. What is the simplest way to reduce the database cost significantly?
options: A. Disable Multi-AZ and automated backups.
B. Move the database to a single EC2 instance running MySQL.
C. Switch to a much smaller instance class without testing.
D. Purchase an RDS Reserved Instance (or use Savings Plans where applicable) for the instance class and Region in use.

question: An application generates a large number of small log files that are written to S3 every few seconds. The company has noticed high request costs (PUT requests). How can the cost of writing the logs be reduced?
options: A. Write the logs to an EBS volume instead of S3.

B. Buffer the log records and write larger objects less frequently (for example using Kinesis Data Firehose with S3 as the destination, or an application-side buffer), and consider using S3 Intelligent-Tiering or lifecycle policies for the resulting objects.
C. Continue writing every small file individually.
D. Disable logging entirely.

question: A company has a large number of Amazon EBS snapshots that are no longer needed. They also have unattached EBS volumes. What actions will reduce storage costs?
options: A. Leave all snapshots and volumes in place indefinitely.
B. Move all snapshots to S3 Glacier manually without a lifecycle policy.

C. Delete unnecessary snapshots and unattached volumes. Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (DLM) or AWS Backup policies to automate retention going forward. Consider converting gp2 volumes to gp3 for better price/performance.
D. Create more frequent snapshots of every volume.

question: A serverless application uses AWS Lambda and Amazon API Gateway. The functions are invoked infrequently but the team has configured provisioned concurrency for all of them at a high level. The bill is higher than expected. What should be reviewed?
options: A. Replace Lambda with always-on EC2 instances.
B. Increase provisioned concurrency further to improve performance.

C. Right-size or remove unnecessary provisioned concurrency; use it only for functions that truly require consistent low latency and have predictable traffic. For spiky or low-traffic functions, on-demand concurrency is usually more cost-effective.
D. Switch every function to the maximum memory setting.

question: A company is using NAT Gateways in every Availability Zone for a large number of private subnets. The data transfer and hourly charges for the NAT Gateways are significant. What are valid cost-optimization strategies?
options: A. Keep a NAT Gateway in every AZ regardless of actual traffic patterns.
B. Replace all NAT Gateways with internet gateways on private subnets.

C. Evaluate whether VPC endpoints (gateway endpoints for S3/DynamoDB, interface endpoints for other services) can eliminate the need for NAT for a large portion of the traffic; consider a shared NAT Gateway design where appropriate; review whether all subnets truly need outbound internet access.
D. Disable all private subnet route tables.

question: An organization wants to track cost by project, environment (dev/test/prod), and business unit. They currently have no consistent tagging strategy. What is the recommended first step?
options: A. Ignore tagging and only look at the total bill.
B. Use only the AWS Free Tier and avoid any cost analysis.

C. Define a mandatory tagging policy (for example Project, Environment, Owner, CostCenter), enforce it with AWS Organizations Service Control Policies or IAM policies, activate cost allocation tags in Billing, and use Cost Explorer and Cost and Usage Reports to analyze spend by tag.
D. Create a separate AWS account for every project without any tagging.

question: A company has a containerized application running on Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type. The tasks are over-provisioned with CPU and memory. What should the Solutions Architect recommend?
options: A. Move everything back to EC2 without any analysis.
B. Leave the task definitions at their current large sizes.
C. Switch to the largest possible Fargate configuration for every task.
D. Analyze CloudWatch Container Insights or Container Metrics, right-size the task CPU and memory values, and consider Savings Plans for Fargate or Fargate Spot for interruptible workloads.

question: A data warehouse on Amazon Redshift is used heavily during business hours but is almost idle at night and on weekends. How can the company reduce cost while keeping the cluster available when needed?
options: A. Switch to Amazon Athena for all workloads without evaluating query patterns.
B. Delete the cluster every evening and restore from snapshot every morning.
C. Leave the cluster running at full size 24/7.
D. Use Redshift’s pause and resume capability (or Elastic Resize / Classic Resize to a smaller size during off-hours), or consider Redshift Serverless if the usage pattern fits.

question: An organization is transferring large amounts of data from on-premises data centers to Amazon S3. They are currently using the public internet and paying significant egress charges to their ISP as well as experiencing slow transfer rates. Which AWS service can reduce both cost and transfer time for multi-terabyte or petabyte-scale migrations?
options: A. Use only single-threaded SCP over the internet.
B. Continue using the public internet with multiple parallel streams only.
C. Email the data on hard drives without any tracking.

D. Use AWS DataSync or AWS Snow Family devices (Snowball, Snowball Edge, Snowmobile) depending on the data volume and network bandwidth, or establish an AWS Direct Connect connection for ongoing large transfers.

question: An application uses Amazon ElastiCache for Redis. The cache is running on a large node type 24/7, but CloudWatch metrics show that memory utilization is consistently below 30% and CPU is low. What should be done?
options: A. Disable the cache entirely.
B. Increase the node type to the next larger size.
C. Right-size the node type based on the observed utilization, and consider Reserved Nodes if the cache will run continuously for a year or more.
D. Switch to a multi-AZ configuration with three times the capacity without analysis.
